title: Issue visualizing Depth image in rviz2
body:
## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 22.04
* Binary build
* Version: Fortress version 6.16.0 and ROS2 Humble

## Description
* Expected behavior: 
I try to add the depth sensors in the sdf of my robot in order to have the depth image available in ROS2.
* Actual behavior:
I have the good output for the depth image in Gazebo Image display viewer:
![Screenshot from 2024-09-27 10-04-00](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edc7795a-1271-4182-af57-663ff0379d3a)

But when I visualize it in rviz2 the image is fully black or is in reverse color pattern in function of the settings:
![Screenshot from 2024-09-27 10-20-57](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adc9db9d-f688-4264-bf51-a29efc449848)

![Screenshot from 2024-09-27 10-19-18](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dad16a04-332a-4c36-9fe4-fb8c915041ad)


## Steps to reproduce

I have implement the sensor in this way in my model.sdf:
`

        <sensor name="camera_center" type="depth_camera">
          <gz_frame_id>camera_base_link</gz_frame_id>
          <always_on>1</always_on>
          <update_rate>30</update_rate>
          <visualize>0</visualize>
          <topic>/model/diff_drive/depth_camera</topic>
          <pose>0 0 0 0 -0 0</pose>
          <camera name="camera">
            <horizontal_fov>1</horizontal_fov>
            <image>
              <width>640</width>
              <height>360</height>
              <format>RGB_INT8</format>
            </image>
            <clip>
              <near>0.3</near>
              <far>50.0</far>
            </clip>
          </camera>
      </sensor>

`
I have this for the bridge:
`
- ros_topic_name: "/depth"
  gz_topic_name: "/model/diff_drive/depth_camera"
  ros_type_name: "sensor_msgs/msg/Image"
  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.Image"
  direction: GZ_TO_ROS
`

I'm not sure if the difference come from the encoding, the bridge or simply the rviz2 configuration (if it is it could be interesting to know the default settings to visualize the data).

title: Non-zero Tx values with multiple cameras
body:
<!-- If you're not sure whether your problem is a bug, please ask a question at
https://robotics.stackexchange.com instead.-->

## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04 
* binary build version: 8.7.0

## Description
* Expected behavior: <!-- Tell us what you expected to happen -->

`Tx` should be zero for all cameras.

* Actual behavior: <!-- What happened instead -->

When placing multiple cameras with different frames in Gz, 
the `Tx` value of the second and subsequent cameras does not become zero,
even though they are ideal cameras without distortion.


## Steps to reproduce
<!-- Provide steps so we can try to reproduce this issue -->

1. Place two or more cameras in Gazebo, each assigned to a separate frame.  
2. Use `gz topic -e` to check the Tx values for each camera.

## Output
<!-- Provide screenshots, console logs, backtraces, and/or anything that could
be useful to us resolving this issue -->

camera info 1

title: Provide a way to set  the optical frame convention used for rendering sensors
body:
## Desired behavior
Currently, Gazebo uses the +x forward convention for all rendering sensors. This was done to keep the same behavior as Gazebo Classic. However, this is at odds with the convention in ROS, which is `+z` forward.  Users run into this issue (e.g. https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/issues/29) and the current workaround is to set a static transform in ROS to create a separate optical frame. There's an old PR in https://github.com/gazebosim/ros_gz/pull/257 to add a dedicated publisher, but I think it would be best if Gazebo itself provided a way to set the convention used. 

## Implementation suggestion
We could do one of the following:

1. Add an SDFormat tag to all rendering sensors that sets whether the `+z` convention should be used.
2. Add an SDFormat under `<sensor>` that sets whether the `+z` convention should be used. This would be easier since we'd only modify one SDFormat description file, but it would affect all sensors
3. One of the two options above, but the tag would allow setting a custom transformation matrix.

title: improve IMU downsampling
body:
## Desired behavior
The IMU signal behaves similarly to what one would expect on a real-world IMU. Some noise due to erratic movements of the robot, but nothing large. Example (produced with patched Gazebo):
![gazebo_imu_with_lp](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f8acf28-2f60-41fe-9d8a-f77dcb4dc661)

## Observed behavior
The IMU signal is noisy AF, not at all representative of the actual movements of the robot. Example, and please note the difference between the y-axis scale of this graph and the previous one (produced with current Gazebo Harmonic):
![gazebo_imu_default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/73d0833e-2bea-4792-8189-f1174226578b)

In the example above, the IMU frequency was set to 5 Hz and the simulation step period to 3 ms.

## Reason for the observed behavior
_Note: I'm new to the Gazebo source code, so please correct me where I'm wrong!_

Gazebo calculates accelerations and velocities for each object instance at each timestep. For the IMU sensor, it takes the values of these every `n` steps, with `n` = `simulation_step_rate` / `sensor_readout_rate` and publishes them.

For many sensors, taking the instantaneous value makes sense. However, for the angular velocity and linear acceleration of an IMU it does not, as real-life IMU's don't work like that. In real-life IMU's, the physically occurring velocities and accelerations get low-pass filtered (on the analog and/or digital level) before being published at a low rate. See for example [the datasheet of the popular BMI088](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/media/boschsensortec/downloads/datasheets/bst-bmi088-ds001.pdf), section 4.4: for an output rate (ODR) of 12.5 Hz, the analog signal gets low-pass filtered to 5 Hz (3 dB cutoff frequency).

This explains the mismatch between expected and observed behavior: in the Gazebo implementation, severe aliasing happens due to lack of low-pass filtering before downsampling, showing up as noise.

This results in two issues:
- Inner simulation workings show up clearly in the sensor values. The step-to-step noise on the accelerations and velocities calculated by Gazebo varies from situation to situation and depends strongly on simulation settings. On itself that's a non-issue, however, this noise must not show up that severely in sensor readings. Applying a low-pass filter filters out most of this, as the sensor readout frequency tends to be a good bit lower than the simulation step rate.
- High-frequency sensor movement gets aliased on the sensor readings. Even if Gazebo's accelerations and velocities would be perfect (with the noise mentioned above not present), then still the simulated reading wouldn't match well what a real-life IMU sensor would give, because that real-life sensor applies a low-pass filter, avoiding sampling issues. Applying a low-pass filter appropriate for the output data rate avoids this downsampling issue.

## Implementation suggestion
As I believe that this is an important feature for anyone using the IMU sensor, I'm interested in making PRs for this. I'll need some guidance though, as I'm not familiar with the Gazebo codebase and the made assumptions.

Main proposed changes:
- In [src/ImuSensor.cc](src/ImuSensor.cc)
   - Add a method
      ```c++
      void ImuSensor::FilterAndSetAngularVelocityAndLinearAcceleration(
        const math::Vector3d &_angularVel,
        const math::Vector3d &_linearAcc,
        const std::chrono::steady_clock::duration _simTime,
        const std::chrono::steady_clock::duration _readOutPeriod)
      ```
      which updates the velocities and accelerations while applying a low-pass filter, like
      ```
      this->dataPtr->linearAcc = this->dataPtr->linearAcc * beta + _linearAcc * alpha;
      ```
      with `alpha + beta == 1`.
  - Add a class variable `prevSetStep` which keeps track of the last time the above lowpass filter was run.
  - In the `ImuSensor::Update` method, which publishes the Imu message, make a copy of the accelerations and velocities and apply the gravity and the noise on the copies, such that the existing class variables can be used for the low-pass filtering. (These `math::Vector3` objects are small, so the performance impact of a copy is negligible.)
- In [gz-sim:src/systems/imu/imu.cc](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/gz-sim9/src/systems/imu/Imu.cc)
   - In the method `Imu::PostUpdate`, _always_ update the IMU sensor such that the low-pass filter is run. This makes the simulation slightly slower, but I think the resulting fidelity increase makes this change more than worth it (and compared to all the rendering and physics calculations, the overall impact of running this lowpass filter is probably not measurable).
   - The method `ImuPrivate::Update` gets extended with a second argument for the simulation time:
     ```c++
     public: void Update(const EntityComponentManager &_ecm,
        const std::chrono::steady_clock::duration _simTime);
     ```
   - And in that method, we call `ImuSensor::FilterAndSetAngularVelocityAndLinearAcceleration` instead of the current `ImuSensor::SetAngularVelocity` and `ImuSensor::SetLinearAcceleration`. We include the simulation time such that the low-pass filter can calculate the appropriate `alpha`.
- Add to the IMU sensor a parameter `lowpass_cutoff_frequency_ratio` that defaults to 2.5. This is the ratio between the sensor output rate and the 3 dB frequency of the applied low-pass filter. This default matches with what's used in the BMI088 (and likely many other similar devices) and makes sense from a signal processing perspective, providing a reasonable balance between avoiding aliasing without smoothing out and delaying the signal too much.
- And some changes here and there for GUI, SDF etc., haven't looked into that yet in detail.

I'm not sure what Gazebo's way is of handling changes over multiple repositories and avoiding the resulting compatibility conflicts. The proposed above changes in `gz-sim` depend on those in `gz-sensors`, though the other way round there's no compatibility issue.

I'd appreciate feedback on the proposed changes.

## Desired behavior

Some force-torque sensors on the market (such as the [products from ATI](https://www.ati-ia.com/products/ft/ft_Selection.aspx)) have additional parameters that are not currently included in our ForceTorque sensor model:

* built-in low-pass filters with configurable cutoff frequency
* maximum measurable force/torque

We should add these paramters to SDFormat and implement support for them.

## Alternatives considered
<!-- Describe alternate solutions or features you've considered.-->

## Implementation suggestion

expedite this implementation.-->

title: Allow setting IMU orientation covariance
body:
Currently, Gazebo/SDF do not allow IMU orientation pose to have a covariance (all zeros are set).
Is there any plan to allow setting covariance values?

A lot of commercial IMUs feature internal orientation estimation filters nowadays, so there should be a way to have a simulation where a sensor with the same outputs (and related properties) can be used.

Otherwise, pose estimation filters (like `fuse`) do not accept orientation inputs with 0 covariance, and different configurations for real robot & simulator have to be managed.

title: Examples should use FindElement instead of GetElement
body: `GetElement` creates a new element if none is found, but that doesn't make sense when it has already been checked to exist. Also when it used without checking existence (by mistake) it can cause "Error [Utils.cc:176] Missing element description for [<tag>]" which I found to be particularly difficult to track.

title: Custom GpuLidarSensor implementation with 'time' field
body:
### TLDR
Is there an easy way to implement a custom Plugin, like Odometer.cc, but inheriting from Lidar class, without building from source?

-----------

Hi everyone!

I'm working on a project where we want to perform SLAM with a robot equipped with a Velodyne Lidar. 
We ported the simulation from Gazebo Classic to Gazebo Fortress (__ign-sensors6__ branch), however in this simulator the fields that are published by GpuLidarSensor are not the same as in Gazebo Classic. 
Basically we're missing the "time" field for each point. Was this field removed because now points are obtained all at the same time, rather than one-by-one?

Adding the whole gz-sensors repo to build from source did not make sense as we only need to modify one sensor.
In any case, we expect the physical Velodyne Lidar to actually publish the timestamps for each point, so I thought I'd make a custom plugin as shown with the Odometer sensor.

In this case however, rather than inheriting from Sensor I'd inherit from Lidar and have a very similar code to _GpuLidarSensor.cc_. However, when  ```this->Lidar::Load(_sdf)``` is called during the initialization, the following errors are obtained:

```
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] [Err] [Lidar.cc:113] Attempting to a load a Lidar sensor, but received a custom
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] [Err] [Lidar.cc:119] Attempting to a load a Lidar sensor, but received a null sensor.
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] [Err] [SensorFactory.hh:105] Failed to load sensor [b2::b2/base_link::b2/CustomGpuLidarSensor] of type[custom]
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] Failed to create lidar
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] [Err] [LidarSystem.cc:83] Failed to create lidar [b2::b2/base_link::b2/CustomGpuLidarSensor]
```

I've tried using ```this->Sensor::Load(_sdf)``` instead, which also required manually setting ```this->Scene()``` (callback ```ConnectSceneChangeCallback(...)``` kept ```this->Scene()``` with a value of 0). Then I would set all possible variables from the sdf to the GpuRaysPtr variable, but would ultimately meet another error:

```
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Ogre::InternalErrorException'
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1]   what():  OGRE EXCEPTION(7:InternalErrorException): Cannot create GL vertex buffer in GLHardwareVertexBuffer::GLHardwareVertexBuffer at ./RenderSystems/GL/src/OgreGLHardwareVertexBuffer.cpp (line 45)
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] Stack trace (most recent call last) in thread 15238:
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] #28   Object "[0xffffffffffffffff]", at 0xffffffffffffffff, in 
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] #27   Object "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6", at 0x7ee27892684f, in 

. . .

[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] #0    Object "/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6", at 0x7ee2788969fc, in pthread_kill
[ruby $(which ign) gazebo-1] Aborted (Signal sent by tkill() 15097 1000)
```

After getting this error I backtracked and just implemented a ROS2 node that takes the pointcloud published by the 'onboard' _GpuLidarSensor.cc_, adds the time field and republishes it. However it seems like a waste of CPU and seems like a less elegant solution.

Am I giving up too early or is there any way to instantiate a sensor of type gpu_lidar whilst also being of type "custom"?

If I can provide any further info, code, appreciation for your work, let me know :)

Thanks in advance!

PS: I must load "ignition::gazebo::systems::Sensors" as I need the plugin for other sensors.

title: Clarify min and max temperature of thermal camera
body:
This is an attempt to improve the documentation of the `<min_temp>`, `<max_temp>` and `<resolution>` tags in the thermal camera documentation.

After reading the description of `<min_temp>` and `<max_temp>` in the thermal camera tutorial I expected an output camera image value of `0` to mean `<min_temp>` Kelvin and a value of `2^bitDepth - 1` to mean `<max_temp>` Kelvin, so I was surprised to find out that that was not the case. Granted, the presence of the `<resolution>` tag did not really fit this mental model. It is also possible that this confusion was amplified by bugs that are now fixed (https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1133 and https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1138).

Nevertheless I tried to rephrase the descriptions a bit in an attempt to minimize the potential for confusion in the future. Hopefully it makes some sense to people other than me.

title: air_pressure sensor does not respect world elevation
body:
**Problem**
The `air_pressure` sensor defaults to 0. I think it would be more intuitive if the air pressure tracked the elevation of the world + model pose.
```
pressure = elevation * pascal_per_meter_air + model_pose.z * pascal_per_meter_air
```

I noticed there's a `reference_altitude` field in `air_pressure`, but populating this value doesn't change anything. The reported pressure is still always the same at 0. But, I don't think this should be set manually anyway.

**Use case**
My world file specifies coordinates
```
    <spherical_coordinates>
      <surface_model>EARTH_WGS84</surface_model>
      <world_frame_orientation>ENU</world_frame_orientation>
      <latitude_deg>47.397971057728974</latitude_deg>
      <longitude_deg> 8.546163739800146</longitude_deg>
      <elevation>40</elevation>
    </spherical_coordinates>
```
and I am using an `air_pressure` sensor on a drone as the barometer. 
```
      <sensor name="air_pressure_sensor" type="air_pressure">
        <always_on>1</always_on>
        <update_rate>50</update_rate>
        <air_pressure>
          <!-- Noise modeled after BMP390 -->
          <pressure>
            <noise type="gaussian">
              <stddev>3</stddev>
            </noise>
          </pressure>
        </air_pressure>
      </sensor>
```

title: Clarify min and max temperature of thermal camera (backport #523)
body:
This is an attempt to improve the documentation of the `<min_temp>`, `<max_temp>` and `<resolution>` tags in the thermal camera documentation.

After reading the description of `<min_temp>` and `<max_temp>` in the thermal camera tutorial I expected an output camera image value of `0` to mean `<min_temp>` Kelvin and a value of `2^bitDepth - 1` to mean `<max_temp>` Kelvin, so I was surprised to find out that that was not the case. Granted, the presence of the `<resolution>` tag did not really fit this mental model. It is also possible that this confusion was amplified by bugs that are now fixed (https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1133 and https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1138).

Nevertheless I tried to rephrase the descriptions a bit in an attempt to minimize the potential for confusion in the future. Hopefully it makes some sense to people other than me.

title: Gazebo Harmonic RGBD Camera: PointCloud and Depth Data Misaligned
body:
**Note 1** 
I posted this question on [Robotics Stackexchange](https://robotics.stackexchange.com/questions/117138/gazebo-harmonic-rgbd-camera-pointcloud-and-depth-data-misaligned) last week, sorry for reposting here



**Note 2**
I created a repo with a minimal, reproducible example to help investigate the suspected issue https://github.com/miccol/rgbd_camera_issue

I'm using the `rgbd_camera` plugin in **Gazebo Harmonic** with ROS 2 and `ros_gz_bridge` to visualize RGB and depth data in RViz. 


Here's my setup:

 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04
 - ROS 2: Jazzy
 - Gazebo: Harmonic 8.9.0

The setup publishes the following topics:

- `/rgbd_camera/camera_info` (`sensor_msgs/CameraInfo`)
- `/rgbd_camera/depth_image` (`sensor_msgs/Image`)
- `/rgbd_camera/image` (`sensor_msgs/Image`)
- `/rgbd_camera/points` (`sensor_msgs/PointCloud2`)

### The (Potential) Issue

Although both `/camera_info` and `/points` have the **same frame\_id** (`rgbd_camera_link`), in RViz the **camera pyramid (from CameraInfo)** and the **PointCloud2** are **visually misaligned**.

The point cloud appears skewed or offset from the expected camera frustum. All TFs are valid, and static transforms are correctly set.

[![enter image description here][1]][1]

[![screenshot][2]][2]
### What I've Checked

* Confirmed both messages use the same `frame_id`
* TF tree is consistent and stable
* RViz Fixed Frame is `world`
* Camera is static and aligned properly
* RGB image renders fine
* PointCloud renders fine
* CameraInfo  renders fine

### My Hypothesis

There may be a mismatch in the **projection model** used internally by the `rgbd_camera` plugin to compute the point cloud vs. what's reported in `/camera_info`.

Alternatively, it could be a bug in how Gazebo Harmonic or `ros_gz_bridge` constructs the `PointCloud2` message.

---

**Question:**

Has anyone seen this misalignment issue between `camera_info` and point clouds from `rgbd_camera` in Gazebo Harmonic?

Could this be due to an internal projection inconsistency or a known bug in `gz-sensors`?
It looks like that, recently, someone else had a similar issue https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/issues/29#issuecomment-3113732696

https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/issues/3042

Thanks

MC


  [1]: https://i.sstatic.net/AJUhxOb8.png
  [2]: https://i.sstatic.net/9QX5EwEK.png

title: Recreating DepthCamera sensor in the same scene causes crash
body:
<!-- If you're not sure whether your problem is a bug, please ask a question at
https://robotics.stackexchange.com instead.-->

## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 22.04
* Source or binary build?
  Binary, gz-sim9
## Description
* Expected behavior: We should be able to remove and create sensors without causing crash
* Actual behavior: When removing a DepthCamera sensor using SensorManager and recreating it from the same SDF, the program crashes with the following error:
 ``` ./OgreMain/src/OgreHlmsDatablock.cpp:199: virtual Ogre::HlmsDatablock::~HlmsDatablock(): Assertion `mLinkedRenderables.empty() && "This Datablock is still being used by some Renderables." " Change their Datablocks before destroying this."' failed.```
Note that this issue doesn't occur wth other sensor types (RGB for example).

## Steps to reproduce
<!-- Provide steps so we can try to reproduce this issue -->

1. Minimal reproduction code
```cpp
#include <iostream>
#include <thread>
#include <chrono>

#include <sdf/Sensor.hh>
#include <gz/common/Console.hh>
#include <gz/rendering/RenderingIface.hh>
#include <gz/rendering/RenderEngine.hh>
#include <gz/rendering/Scene.hh>
#include <gz/sensors/Manager.hh>
#include <gz/sensors/DepthCameraSensor.hh>

static sdf::Sensor MakeDepthCamSdf()
{
    sdf::Sensor s;
    s.SetName("repro_depth");
    s.SetType(sdf::SensorType::DEPTH_CAMERA);

    sdf::Camera *cam = new sdf::Camera();
    cam->SetImageWidth(320);
    cam->SetImageHeight(240);
    cam->SetFarClip(10.0);
    cam->SetNearClip(0.1);
    cam->SetHorizontalFov(gz::math::Angle::HalfPi);
    s.SetCameraSensor(*cam);

    // Minimal update rate so we create renderables quickly
    s.SetUpdateRate(30.0);

    return s;
}

static sdf::Sensor MakeRGBCamSdf()
{
    sdf::Sensor s;
    s.SetName("repro_rgb");
    s.SetType(sdf::SensorType::CAMERA);

    sdf::Camera *cam = new sdf::Camera();
    cam->SetImageWidth(320);
    cam->SetImageHeight(240);
    cam->SetFarClip(10.0);
    cam->SetNearClip(0.1);
    cam->SetHorizontalFov(gz::math::Angle::HalfPi);
    s.SetCameraSensor(*cam);

    // Minimal update rate so we create renderables quickly
    s.SetUpdateRate(30.0);

    return s;
}

struct SceneManager{
    SceneManager(std::string engineName="ogre2"):engineName(engineName){
        engine = gz::rendering::engine(engineName);
        if (!engine){
            throw std::runtime_error("couldnt create engine with name "+engineName);
        }
        scene = engine->CreateScene("repro_scene");
        if (!scene){
            throw std::runtime_error("couldnt create scene");
        }
        scene->SetBackgroundColor(gz::math::Color(0.1f, 0.1f, 0.1f));
    };
    ~SceneManager(){
        engine->DestroyScene(scene);
        gz::rendering::unloadEngine(engineName);
    };
    gz::rendering::RenderEngine* engine;
    const std::string engineName = "ogre2";
    gz::rendering::ScenePtr scene;
};

int main()
{
    gz::common::Console::SetVerbosity(4);
    SceneManager scene_mgr;
    gz::sensors::Manager mgr;
    auto sdf_ = MakeRGBCamSdf();
    // first rgb camera test
    // each iteration will create and then destory sensor
    for (int k =0; k<3; ++k){    
        auto *base = mgr.CreateSensor<gz::sensors::CameraSensor>(sdf_);
        auto *rgb = dynamic_cast<gz::sensors::CameraSensor*>(base);
        rgb->SetScene(scene_mgr.scene);
        rgb->SetParent("repro_link");
        auto conn = rgb->ConnectImageCallback(
            [](const gz::msgs::Image &)
            {
            // no-op
            });
        for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i){
                mgr.RunOnce(std::chrono::steady_clock::duration(std::chrono::milliseconds(16)));
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
        }
    {
    auto renderCam = rgb->RenderingCamera();
    if (renderCam)
    {
        std::cout << "[Repro] Destroying RGBCamera render object directly...\n";
        renderCam->Destroy();
    }

    std::cout << "[Repro] Removing sensor from Manager...\n";
    mgr.Remove(rgb->Id());
        }
    }
    // next depth camera test
    sdf_ = MakeDepthCamSdf();
    for (int k =0; k<3; ++k){    
        auto *base = mgr.CreateSensor<gz::sensors::DepthCameraSensor>(sdf_);
        auto *depth = dynamic_cast<gz::sensors::DepthCameraSensor*>(base);
        depth->SetScene(scene_mgr.scene);
        depth->SetParent("repro_link");
        auto conn = depth->ConnectImageCallback(
            [](const gz::msgs::Image &)
            {
            // no-op
            });
        for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i){
                mgr.RunOnce(std::chrono::steady_clock::duration(std::chrono::milliseconds(16)));
                std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(1));
        }
    {
    auto renderCam = depth->DepthCamera();
    if (renderCam)
    {
        std::cout << "[Repro] Destroying DepthCamera render object directly...\n";
        renderCam->Destroy();
    }

    std::cout << "[Repro] Removing sensor from Manager...\n";
    mgr.Remove(depth->Id());
        }
    }

    std::cout << "Done.\n";
    return 0;
}
```

title: RGBD and Depth camera plugins setting is_dense to True, even when point cloud has invalid points (inf)
body:
## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04
* Sim: Binary Build 8.10.0 (Harmonic)

## Description
Similar issue to #179. RGBDCameraSensor and DepthCameraSensor set the `is_dense` flag is set to true regardless of whether the point cloud only contains valid points or not (inf/NaN). 
* Expected behavior: `is_dense` flag is set to `False` if the data contains inf or NaN.
* Actual behavior: inf is found in the data, but `is_dense` is True

## Steps to Reproduce
1. In a terminal, run [sensors_demo.sdf](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/blob/gz-sim8/examples/worlds/sensors_demo.sdf)
```bash
gz sim sensors_demo.sdf -r
```
2. In another terminal, run
```bash
ros2 run ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge /depth_camera/points@sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2[gz.msgs.PointCloudPacked /rgbd_camera/points@sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2[gz.msgs.PointCloudPacked
```
to bridge the cloud topics to ROS

3. In a third terminal, run 
```bash
ros2 topic echo /depth_camera/points --once
```
or
```bash
ros2 topic echo /rgbd_camera/points --once
```

## Output
The output of step 3 is the following:
```bash
...
fields:
- name: x
  offset: 0
  datatype: 7
  count: 1
...
is_bigendian: false
...
data:
- 0
- 0
- 128
- 127
...
is_dense: true
```

The first couple of elements represent an instance of field `x`,  which has a datatype 7 ([FLOAT32](https://docs.ros.org/en/noetic/api/sensor_msgs/html/msg/PointField.html)). The data is represented in [UINT8](https://docs.ros.org/en/noetic/api/sensor_msgs/html/msg/PointCloud2.html), so to convert the raw data into FLOAT32, the first 4 elements are concatenated in the following order `[127, 128, 0, 0]` (little endian). This results in a 32 bit number representing `0x7F800000`, which is +inf in FLOAT32. 

Since the data contains +inf, this should be indicated by is_dense being false. This causes issues with [PCL](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/issues/176#issuecomment-993086307).

title: Add custom point cloud frame ID support to Depth and RGBD camera sensors
body:
<!--
Please remove the appropriate section.
For example, if this is a new feature, remove all sections except for the "New feature" section

If this is your first time opening a PR, be sure to check the contribution guide:
https://gazebosim.org/docs/all/contributing
-->

# 🎉 New feature

Closes #488 

## Summary
**The problem**
Currently, the depth and rgbd cameras use the content from the `<frame_id>` tag or the default frameId for both the 
the images and the point cloud. However, the images typically need an optical frame id while the point cloud needs a "sensor" frame id. 

**The Solution**
This proposed change enables depth and rbgd camera sensors to include a new `<points_frame_id>` tag to use for the point cloud messages. This is not a breaking change, because when the tag is not included, behavior is unchanged.

Example:
```xml
      <sensor name="camera_with_points_frame_id" type="depth">
        <update_rate>10</update_rate>
        <frame_id>optical_frame</frame_id>
        <points_frame_id>points_frame</points_frame_id>
        <topic>/camera2/image</topic>
        <camera>
          <horizontal_fov>1.0472</horizontal_fov>
          <image>
            <width>1000</width>
            <height>1000</height>
          </image>
          <lens>
            <projection>
              <p_fx>866.23</p_fx>
              <p_fy>866.23</p_fy>
              <p_cx>500</p_cx>
              <p_cy>500</p_cy>
              <tx>300</tx>
              <ty>200</ty>
            </projection>
          </lens>
        </camera>
      </sensor>
 ```

## Test it
To test manually, launch gazebo sim with a urdf containing a depth camera that uses the new tag. Then verify frame ids on the images and point clouds are correct.

title: Add CpuLidarSensor for physics-based lidar without rendering
body:
# 🎉 New feature

This PR is 2 out of 3 that implement: https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/issues/26

## Summary

Add `CpuLidarSensor`, a new sensor class that extends `gz::sensors::Sensor` directly (not `RenderingSensor`), receives raycast results from a system plugin, applies noise, and publishes `LaserScan` and `PointCloudPacked` messages over gz-transport. Zero dependency on `gz-rendering`.

The existing `GpuLidarSensor` requires Ogre2 and a GPU, making it unusable on headless cloud machines, containers, and CI/CD environments. Gazebo Classic had a CPU-based `RaySensor` backed by the physics engine; this is the new-architecture
equivalent.

`CpuLidarSensor` extends `Sensor` instead of the existing `Lidar` class because `Lidar` extends `RenderingSensor`, which would pull in `gz-rendering` as a transitive dependency. The SDF parsing, noise application, and message publishing logic is reimplemented without that dependency.

`GenerateRays()` produces entity-frame ray pairs from the SDF lidar configuration. `SetRaycastResults()` accepts fractions from the physics engine and converts them to ranges (`fraction × ray_length`). Misses (NaN fraction) produce `+inf` per REP-117. For 3D scans with multiple vertical layers, `LaserScan` publishes the middle ring as a 2D slice while `PointCloudPacked` publishes all rings.

## Test it

```bash
colcon build --merge-install --packages-select gz-sensors \
  --cmake-args '-DBUILD_TESTING=ON'
colcon test --packages-select gz-sensors \
  --ctest-args -R INTEGRATION_cpu_lidar_sensor
```

title: Support for lidar dual returns (and multiple?)
body:
## Desired behavior
The lidar sensor supports returning dual (or multiple) returns.

## Alternatives considered
There are no good alternatives.

## Implementation suggestion
Does anybody have an idea how this could be implemented? Have you seen any implementations?

For GPU lidar, I think it would need some quite advanced work with the depth buffer.

For raycasting lidars (once they're merged here), it could be a bit easier, but still some work.

It would also mean that the output of the lidar sensor would either be two (or multiple) pointcloud topics, or that the pointcloud being published would have to have the additional returns encoded into extra channels (this is preferable I think).

## Additional context
E.g. Ouster OS-X Rev 6+ support dual returns. They offer multiple ordering options: STRONGEST_TO_WEAKEST, FURTHEST_TO_NEAREST, NEAREST_TO_FURTHEST. I think this ordering is just a minor implementation effort compared to the rendering part.

Even the old 2D lidar Sick LMS-151 can return dual returns. In our ancient fork https://github.com/peci1/LMS1xx/blob/c999ab90e059dc51dddd6f5ff578bb15e8de7733/src/LMS1xx_nodelet.cpp#L67 we published the second return as a separate LaserScan message, but I don't think that's necessary.

title: Update classes to use gz::utils::UniqueImplPtr
body:
We currently use `std::unique_ptr`s to implement the [pimpl](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/pimpl.html) pattern in the gz-sensors codebase. Example:
https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/blob/3b9b02090d2aec1159069067044364ba198d59b3/include/gz/sensors/Lidar.hh#L277-L281

The `GZ_UTILS_UNIQUE_IMPL_PTR` macro and the underlying `gz::utils::UniqueImplPtr` class encapsulates a lot of the boilerplate for properly implementing the pimpl pattern and should be used to replace all the `std::unique_ptr`s in gz-sensors. Similar work has been done in other parts of the Gazebo codebase (e.g. https://github.com/gazebosim/sdformat/pull/474).

title: Use GTEST_SKIP in unsupported tests
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Part of https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/issues/1235

## Summary

While checking whether `gz-sensors` tests are using ogre2 on macOS, I noticed that very few tests are using `GTEST_SKIP()` for unsupported engines, so this switches the `gzdbg` stream then `return` pattern to stream directly to `GTEST_SKIP()` as is [done in gz-rendering](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/blob/15a0455307f002e9a5e1415198ebbd7ab5731c1b/test/common_test/CommonRenderingTest.hh#L101).

On Ubuntu, this shows an [increase of 1 skipped test](https://build.osrfoundation.org/job/gz_sensors-ci-pr_any-noble-amd64/155/testReport/(root)/):
* [DistortionCameraSensor/DistortionCameraSensorTest.ImagesWithBuiltinSDF/ogre2](https://build.osrfoundation.org/job/gz_sensors-ci-pr_any-noble-amd64/156/testReport/(root)/DistortionCameraSensor_DistortionCameraSensorTest/ImagesWithBuiltinSDF_ogre2/)

On macOS, there are [many new skipped tests](https://build.osrfoundation.org/job/gz_sensors-ci-pr_any-homebrew-arm64/60/testReport/(root)/) due to the removal of `ogre1.9` in https://github.com/osrf/homebrew-simulation/pull/3394 (see follow-up work in #605).

This also fixes a segfault of `INTEGRATION_dvl` when the render engine plugin fails to load, which also started failing on macOS when `ogre1.9` was removed in https://github.com/osrf/homebrew-simulation/pull/3394.

title: Wrong sampling for IMU under the dynamic bias's covariance
body:
<!-- If you're not sure whether your problem is a bug, please ask a question at
https://robotics.stackexchange.com instead.-->

## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 24<!-- e.g, Ubuntu 20.04 -->
* Both source and binary build in all versions
  <!-- If binary, which version? -->
  <!-- If source, which branch and what is the latest commit? -->

## Description
In the file src/GaussianNoiseModel.cc, the derivation of sigma_b_d may be wrong:
`double sigma_b_d = sqrt(-sigma_b * sigma_b * tau / 2 * expm1(-2 * _dt / tau));`
The correct expression which I have verify thorgh Deepseek is 
`double sigma_b_d = sqrt(-sigma_b * sigma_b * expm1(-2 * _dt / tau));`
or simplely
`double sigma_b_d = sigma_b * sqrt(-expm1(-2 * _dt / tau));`
This issue appears in both gyroscope and accelerometer's sampling process.

After I find this issue and multiply a factor `1 / sqrt(tau / 2)` in my EKF algorithm, it goes well in the state prediction with correct covariance propagation.

# 🎉 New feature

Backport of #593 (`CpuLidarSensor`) to the `gz-sensors10` LTS branch. Depends on [PR 1 (gz-physics9)](https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-physics/pull/1027).

## Summary

`CpuLidarSensor` publishes `LaserScan` and `PointCloudPacked` from raycast results with zero dependency on `gz-rendering`, so it runs headless where `GpuLidarSensor` cannot. The only change over a verbatim cherry-pick of #593 is one line, because gz-physics9 reports a miss as `NaN` while gz-physics10 reports `+INF`:

```diff
-    if (std::isinf(_results[i].fraction))
+    if (!std::isfinite(_results[i].fraction))
```

With `std::isinf`, a `NaN` miss on gz-physics9 takes the hit path and publishes a `NaN` range instead of `+inf`. `!std::isfinite` is true for both `NaN` and `+INF`, so it is correct on both.

title: ThermalCameraSensor (and SegmentationCameraSensor) leak message header 'data' entries every frame — unbounded memory growth and progressive sim slowdown
body:
## Summary

`ThermalCameraSensor::Update()` reuses a member `msgs::Image thermalMsg` across
frames and calls `mutable_header()->add_data()` on every update without clearing
previous entries:

```cpp
// src/ThermalCameraSensor.cc (gz-sensors8, still present on main)
auto frame = this->dataPtr->thermalMsg.mutable_header()->add_data();
frame->set_key("frame_id");
frame->add_value(this->FrameId());
```

The header grows by one `data` entry per rendered frame, so:

- protobuf serialization of each published frame costs O(N) in the number of
  frames rendered so far (O(N²) cumulative) — the simulation RTF decays over
  minutes, proportionally to the thermal update rate;
- process RSS grows without bound (~45 KB/frame measured, message + per-publish
  serialization buffers).

`SegmentationCameraSensor` has the same defect on its member `coloredMapMsg`
(src/SegmentationCameraSensor.cc). The same bug family was already fixed for
Lidar (`laserMsg`), LogicalCameraSensor and, recently, BoundingBoxCameraSensor
(#624) — the thermal and segmentation sensors were missed.

## Reproduction (gz-sensors 8.2.2, gz-sim 8.14, Ubuntu 24.04, ogre2/llvmpipe)

Minimal world: empty world + one static box with the Thermal system
(temperature 350) + one static `thermal_camera` sensor, 320x240 L16,
`update_rate` 250 (high rate only to accelerate the effect; it reproduces at
30–60 Hz over longer sessions). Subscribe so the sensor renders:

    gz sim -r -s minithermal.sdf &
    gz topic -e -t /thermal > /dev/null

Observed (28 s sampling of `/world/.../stats` and RSS):

| | start | ~5 min | ~12 min |
|---|---|---|---|
| unpatched RTF | 1.000 | 1.000 → collapse begins | ~0.65 (dips to 0.33) |
| unpatched RSS | 394 MB | ~2.5 GB | 6.3 GB |
| patched RTF | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |
| patched RSS | 386 MB | 382 MB | 382 MB |

gdb sampling of the degraded process shows the render thread dominated by
`gz::msgs::Header_Map::ByteSizeLong` / `_InternalSerialize` /
`VerifyUtf8String` under `ThermalCameraSensor::Update → Publisher::Publish`,
i.e. serialization of the ever-growing header, not rendering.

## Fix

Mirror the existing Lidar/LogicalCamera fix — clear before adding:

```cpp
// Remove 'data' entries before adding new ones
this->dataPtr->thermalMsg.mutable_header()->clear_data();
auto frame = this->dataPtr->thermalMsg.mutable_header()->add_data();
```

and the analogous line for `coloredMapMsg` in `SegmentationCameraSensor`.
Verified locally on gz-sensors8_8.2.2: RTF and RSS stay flat (table above).

title: Test GPU lidar point clouds at cubemap endpoints
body:
## Problem

The GPU lidar point-cloud integration coverage checks message fields and
dimensions, but it does not verify that published XYZ points conform to the
surface that produced their ranges. This left the endpoint regression reported
in https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sim/issues/3475 uncovered.

## Change

Add an Ogre2 point-cloud regression using the reported scan shape:

- 900 horizontal samples from -45 to +45 degrees
- 300 vertical samples from -30 to 0 degrees
- first, middle, and last horizontal columns
- multiple finite vertical rows

The target plane is slightly rolled so the intersection range depends on the
horizontal angle. This prevents an endpoint lookup from wrapping to the
opposite cubemap edge while still appearing correct through plane symmetry.

## Dependency

This test exercises the sampler correction proposed in
https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1319. It should be evaluated with
that renderer branch until the renderer change is merged and released.

## Compatibility

Test-only change. There is no public API, message layout, or runtime behavior
change in this repository.

## Validation

- `git diff --check` passes.
- The configuration and checked point-cloud columns match the reported failure
  boundary.
- GPU lidar integration execution is disabled on macOS, so Linux Ogre2 CI is
  required for runtime validation.

title: Prevent camera frame header accumulation
body:
## Summary

- clear the reused thermal and segmentation image-header `data` fields before
  adding the current `frame_id`
- verify three successive frame IDs never accumulate in thermal images,
  segmentation colored maps, or segmentation label maps
- preserve the existing stamp, image payload, and publish flow

The segmentation label message copies the corrected colored-map message, so
both published outputs now carry exactly one current `frame_id` entry.

Closes #638.

## Regression proof

With the new tests but without the two `clear_data()` calls, both integrations
fail: thermal, colored-map, and label-map header sizes grow from 2 to 3 to 4.
Restoring the fix makes both targeted Ogre2/Xvfb integrations pass.

## Validation

- official-action-equivalent Ubuntu Noble / Rotary dependency environment
- complete build
- cpplint and cppcheck
- full CTest suite: 57/57 passed
- restored targeted camera integrations: 2/2 passed

title: Reject invalid camera clip plane ordering
body:
## Summary

- reject camera configurations whose near clip plane is equal to or farther
  than the far clip plane before sensor initialization
- apply the check in the shared sensor load path so it covers all camera
  sensor implementations
- cover valid ordering, the reported `1e308` / `10.0` values, and equal clip
  planes

This prevents invalid clip values from reaching rendering backends and turns
the reported process abort into an ordinary sensor-load error.

Closes #584.

## Regression proof

The attached issue world reproduces the current binary behavior on Ubuntu
Noble / Gazebo Rotary: `gz sdf -k` reports it as valid, while
`gz sim -r -s` aborts in `Ogre::AxisAlignedBox` with exit 134.

With the new regression but without the validation guard, both invalid cases
load successfully and the test fails. Restoring the guard rejects both cases
with a descriptive error while preserving the valid case.

## Validation

- Ubuntu Noble / Gazebo Rotary dependency environment
- complete build
- full CTest suite: 57/57 passed
- cpplint and cppcheck
- focused regression negative control: failed as expected
- focused regression with the fix: passed

title: Reject invalid camera clip plane ordering (backport #641)
body:
## Summary

- reject camera configurations whose near clip plane is equal to or farther
  than the far clip plane before sensor initialization
- apply the check in the shared sensor load path so it covers all camera
  sensor implementations
- cover valid ordering, the reported `1e308` / `10.0` values, and equal clip
  planes

This prevents invalid clip values from reaching rendering backends and turns
the reported process abort into an ordinary sensor-load error.

Closes #584.

## Regression proof

The attached issue world reproduces the current binary behavior on Ubuntu
Noble / Gazebo Rotary: `gz sdf -k` reports it as valid, while
`gz sim -r -s` aborts in `Ogre::AxisAlignedBox` with exit 134.

With the new regression but without the validation guard, both invalid cases
load successfully and the test fails. Restoring the guard rejects both cases
with a descriptive error while preserving the valid case.

## Validation

- Ubuntu Noble / Gazebo Rotary dependency environment
- complete build
- full CTest suite: 57/57 passed
- cpplint and cppcheck
- focused regression negative control: failed as expected
- focused regression with the fix: passed

title: CameraSensor: render straight into the reused image message payload
body:
# 🎉 New feature

## Summary

This patch is the second half of https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1331 . A camera frame is copied twice on its way out: once from the GPU into a buffer owned by gz-rendering, and once more from that buffer into the `msgs::Image` being published, only because the message needs the bytes in memory it owns. This PR uses the constructor added in gazebosim/gz-rendering#1331 to make the GPU readback land in the message payload directly.

Benchmarked on a world with two 1920x1080 cameras at 30 Hz (headless server, Zenoh with shared memory, interleaved A/B, 3 runs per side, turbo off and no thermal throttling): +18% steps/s and -15% CPU per step. Cameras at 320x240 show no measurable change, since the copy there is about 10 microseconds per frame.

title: Sensor initialization takes very long when `--initial-sim-time` is set to current UNIX timestamp
body:
I think it's because of these lines:

https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-sensors/blob/1449e3eb2d33621b263f80850d1f5d823cdc7c13/src/Sensor.cc#L537-L540

Try with:

    gz sim --initial-sim-time $(date '+%s.0') sensors_demo.sdf

Click Play and wait. It takes 30-60 seconds until the sim actually starts.

When initial sim time is set to 0 (or unset), the start of the simulation is more or less immediate.

My explanation:

`nextUpdateTime` is incremented by very small amounts, starting from 0, until it is greater or equal to `now`. But when `now` is large, this while loop can take a lot of time.

title: Sensor: catch up update schedule in O(1)
body:
Assisted-by: OpenAI ChatGPT GPT-5.6 Sol

# 🦟 Bug fix

Fixes #662

## Summary

Avoid iterating once per missed sensor period when simulation time starts at a large absolute value.

`Sensor::Update()` previously advanced `nextUpdateTime` in a loop until it passed `now`. With a UNIX-scale initial simulation timestamp, that can require billions of iterations.

The same code also truncated the period to whole milliseconds. For update rates above 1000 Hz, that can produce a zero-duration period and a catch-up loop that never makes forward progress.

## Change

- Retain the sensor period in `std::chrono::steady_clock::duration` instead of milliseconds.
- Clamp an unrepresentably small period to one clock tick.
- Replace the linear catch-up loop with O(1) arithmetic.
- Preserve the existing schedule phase: the resulting update time remains the first scheduled tick strictly after `now`.

## Regression coverage

The existing `SensorUpdate.NextDataUpdateTime` test now also covers:

- catching up from a UNIX-scale absolute time;
- a 2000 Hz sub-millisecond update period.

title: CameraSensor: preserve depth projection with custom intrinsics
body:
🦟 Bug fix

Fixes #614

Summary

Preserve depth-camera geometry when explicit lens intrinsics are equivalent to the camera's existing calibration.

"CameraSensor::UpdateLensIntrinsicsAndProjection()" currently rebuilds the full 4×4 projection matrix whenever "<lens><intrinsics>" or "<projection>" is authored.

For depth cameras, the rendering backend may already own depth-specific projection terms. In Ogre / Ogre2, those terms are used by the depth pipeline to linearize depth and reconstruct XYZ point-cloud positions.

Replacing the full matrix from sensor-side calibration therefore couples two separate concerns:

- image-plane calibration: "fx", "fy", "cx", "cy", skew;
- backend-specific depth projection / encoding.

This can leave the published depth image effectively unchanged while changing the reconstructed point cloud, even when the explicitly authored intrinsics are equivalent to the camera's default calibration.

Change

When applying custom intrinsics or projection values:

- rebuild the requested image-plane projection;
- copy only the first two projection-matrix rows, which encode the image-plane calibration;
- preserve the renderer's existing depth-related projection rows.

This keeps the rendering backend's depth mapping intact while still honoring custom camera calibration.

Regression coverage

The existing "DepthCameraIntrinsics" integration test already creates:

1. a depth camera with implicit/default intrinsics;
2. a depth camera with explicitly authored equivalent intrinsics;
3. a camera with intentionally different intrinsics.

The test previously only validated "CameraInfo", despite its comment stating that the first two cameras should produce equivalent images.

This PR extends that invariant to verify that the first two cameras have equivalent:

- projection matrices;
- depth images;
- XYZ point clouds.

The fixture's explicit focal length is also updated to the value implied by the configured horizontal FOV rather than the previous rounded approximation.

Why this belongs in "gz-sensors"

"gz-sensors" translates SDF camera calibration into rendering-camera configuration.

The rendering backend remains responsible for the depth-projection terms required by its depth-buffer and XYZ reconstruction implementation. Applying SDF intrinsics should therefore modify image calibration without silently replacing backend-owned depth encoding.

Validation

The focused regression and fix are included, but were not run locally in the environment used to prepare this contribution because that environment can inspect and write GitHub but cannot clone/build the repository.

CI on this PR is the executable validation.

# 🦟 Bug fix

Related to https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1344

## Summary
`gz-rendering` introduced `PixelBuffer` and `Camera::CopyTo()` for writing frames into caller-owned memory. The raw-pointer `Image` constructor used by `gz-sensors` is no longer public.

As a result, `gz-sensors` fails to compile against the updated `gz-rendering`.

This PR updates `CameraSensor` to pass the image message payload to `Camera::CopyTo()` through a `PixelBuffer`. It removes the obsolete `Image` member and sizes the payload before copying each frame.

title: Load reference_altitude from SDF in AirPressureSensor
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Fixes #531

## Summary
`AirPressureSensor::Load()` never reads `<air_pressure><reference_altitude>` from SDF. The sensor always uses a reference altitude of 0, so the element has no effect. The value can only be changed through `SetReferenceAltitude()` in code.

This change passes the value from `sdf::AirPressure` to the sensor in `Load()`. When the element is not set, the default is still 0, so nothing changes for existing models.

To reproduce: load an `air_pressure` sensor with `<reference_altitude>500</reference_altitude>` and read one message.
- Before: `ReferenceAltitude()` is 0 and the pressure is the sea-level value of the model, 101325 Pa at z = 0.
- After: `ReferenceAltitude()` is 500 and the pressure is 95461.29 Pa.

The new `ReferenceAltitudeFromSdf` test checks both values. It fails without the fix and passes with it.

This covers the `reference_altitude` part of the issue. Taking the world elevation from `<spherical_coordinates>` into account would be a change in the gz-sim system, so it is not part of this PR.

title: Change the horizontal field of view of camera sensors at runtime
body:
# 🎉 New feature

Closes gazebosim/gz-sim#2214

## Summary

Camera sensors can now change their horizontal field of view while the simulation runs, for example to simulate the optical zoom of a PTZ camera.

- `CameraSensor` subscribes to `<topic>/set_hfov` (`gz.msgs.Double`, radians), next to the existing `<topic>/trigger`.
- The transport callback only stores the value under the sensor's mutex. It is applied in the next `Update()`, on the rendering thread.
- The lens intrinsics, the projection and `camera_info` are recomputed with the existing `UpdateLensIntrinsicsAndProjection()` and `PopulateInfo()`, starting from the camera SDF as loaded. They match what a camera created with that field of view publishes.
- Cameras whose SDF sets `<lens><intrinsics>` or `<lens><projection>` keep them, since those define the field of view: the request is ignored with a warning. Out-of-range angles are rejected with the same bounds as at creation.
- No public API or ABI change: the new state lives in the private implementation.

Points I'd like your opinion on:
- The topic is always available on camera sensors. Making it opt-in would need a new SDF element (sdformat); I can add one if you prefer.
- The change is instantaneous (no zoom speed). A plugin can ramp the value if needed.
- Only `CameraSensor` is covered. Depth, RGBD, thermal, wide-angle and the other camera-based sensors are unchanged.

## Backport Policy
- [x] This is safe to backport to the following versions:
    - [x] Jetty
    - [x] Ionic
    - [x] Harmonic
    - [ ] Fortress
- [ ] This **should not** be backported
- [ ] I am not sure
- [ ] Other (fill in yourself)

No API or ABI change. I tested the same patch on top of `gz-sensors8_8.2.2` with Harmonic. Jetty and Ionic were not tested.

## Test it

With the `camera_sensor.sdf` example world (camera topic `camera`, `horizontal_fov` 1.047):

```
gz sim -r camera_sensor.sdf
gz topic -t /camera/set_hfov -m gz.msgs.Double -p 'data: 0.35'
```

The Image Display panel zooms in about 3x. `gz topic -e -t /camera_info` shows `fx` going from 277.2 to 904.9, which is 320 / (2 tan(0.175)). Publish `data: 1.047` to go back to the original view. These numbers come from Harmonic (gz-sim 8.15 with this patch on gz-sensors 8.2.2).

The new integration test `CameraSensorTest.SetHfov` checks the rendering camera's field of view and the `camera_info` intrinsics, and that a camera with lens intrinsics in SDF is left unchanged.

Tested:
- `main`: `INTEGRATION_camera` 6/6, built against gz-rendering `main` (fb8e38c). The current nightly packages are older than the `PixelBuffer` API that `main` already uses.
- Harmonic backport: `INTEGRATION_camera` 5/5.

title: Depth, RGBD and GPU lidar sensors: lower CPU and wall-clock cost without changing the output (PR series and API questions)
body:
## Desired behavior

*The PRs of this series are open as drafts and linked below. Bold labels (**08b**, **09b**, …) are prepared branches that wait on the questions here. The OgreNext PR (**15**) will follow.*

Depth cameras, RGBD cameras and GPU lidars should cost less CPU per simulated second, and let gz-sim run faster at RTF 0, while publishing the same messages as today. Some PRs in this series add public API in gz-rendering, gz-sensors and gz-transport, so I would like to agree on that API before opening them. A few further gains change the output; for those I'd like to know whether you want them at all, as opt-in options.

gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 (readback wait) is already open; the rendering PRs below build on it.

**Setup.** ANYmal on MuJoCo at a 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL. Main scenario: six 640x480 depth cameras at 15 Hz. CPU: gz-sim server CPU seconds per simulated second, pinned to 1 core. Wall: simulated seconds per wall second on 3 cores. Both at RTF 0, n=5 runs of 20 s per arm, arms interleaved, mean ± 95% CI. Base: gz-sensors 8ddf4c1, gz-rendering fb8e38ce, gz-transport 41913b9d, gz-sim 71c60db31.

On main with six depth cameras, physics waits for the render thread 61% of the wall time. Each camera waits for its own GPU-to-CPU transfer in `PostRender()`, one camera after another. A frame with no point cloud subscriber still reads back the full RGBA32F point cloud texture (4.9 MB at 640x480). The sensor then copies the frame two or three more times before the message reaches the transport.

## Changes with byte-identical output (PRs ready)

Each row is one PR measured alone on top of the PRs it needs (the base column). The messages are unchanged; see the next section for how this was checked.

**Render ahead** (overlap the readbacks of several sensors)

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392 (16a) + #697 (16b) | `Camera::IssueReadback()`; `Manager::RunOnce` renders every due depth camera and GPU lidar and issues their readbacks, then runs each `Update()` | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 | depth images −6.9%; with `/points` −9.1%; three 2048x128 lidars −1.3% (noise) | **+39%**; **+40%**; **+13%** |
| #698 (19) | the same for `RgbdCameraSensor` (six 640x480 RGBD cameras) | 16b | image −7.9%; all topics −7.8% | image **+24.5%**; depth **+53.1%**; all topics **+47.2%** |

**Depth camera**

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1393 (07) | with no point cloud subscriber, render and read back only the R32 depth (1.2 MB instead of 4.9 MB), in one quad pass, without unread clears | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 | depth images **−31.6%**; with `/points` no change | **+58%**; no change |
| #699 (08) | `DepthCameraSensor`: copy the frame once, fill the cloud in one pass, publish image and cloud in place (needs 05) | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + 05 | depth images **−12.4%**; `/points` ZeroMQ **−33.2%**, Zenoh **−38.1%** | **+25%**; **+50%**, **+68%** |
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1394 (09a) + **08b** | the rendering camera can deliver packed xyz (12 instead of 16 bytes per point, no colour pass); the sensor asks for it, since its `rgb` field is a grayscale of the depth anyway | 07 / 08 | 09a alone: no change (nothing asks for packed yet) | |

Stack 16 + 07 + 09a + 08 + 08b against main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + 05, depth images and `/points` over Zenoh SHM (64 MiB pool): CPU 0.4134 ± 0.0078 → 0.1825 ± 0.0042 (−56%), wall 2.53 ± 0.08 → 5.76 ± 0.30 (2.3×).

**Publish in place** (gz-transport API and its users)

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (05) | `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`: the caller writes the serialized message straight into the buffer the transport sends | main | no change alone (no caller) | no change |
| #693 (06) | lidar scan and points in place (one 2048x128 lidar) | main + 01 + 02 + 05 | ZeroMQ −6.6%, Zenoh **−6.9%** | not resolved |
| #694 (14) | camera image in place (six 640x480 cameras) | main + 05 | −2.9% (noise) | **+7.0% ± 6.2** |
| #695 (17) | RGBD depth image in place (depth subscribed) | main + 05 | **−10.6%** | **+21.4%** |
| #696 (18) | RGBD point cloud and image in place | 17 | image only **−32.9%**; all topics **−21.7%** | **+20.1%**; +37.8% ± 27.9 |

(08 above is also a user of 05.)

## How equivalence was checked

- gz-sim main with the PRs against unmodified gz-sim main. A sink in another process records every message of every sensor topic; each message's raw bytes are compared by CRC, matched by header stamp.
- Worlds: four depth worlds (static, moving, 16 moving boxes, 16 boxes spawned and removed between renders), three cameras each, depth images and `/points`; three lidar worlds (static, moving, Gaussian noise with a fixed seed); five RGBD worlds (static, moving, transition, noise, toggle). ZeroMQ or Zenoh, as stated in each PR.
- A toggle test: point cloud subscribers connect and leave during the run while a model moves into the forward camera's view. It checks the first cloud after a subscriber connects and the first cloud of the run.
- Each PR has unit or integration tests that fail when its change is perturbed.

**Toggle test start-up.** Earlier toggle runs differed on the forward camera from t=1.667 s on, where the moving model enters its view, also on unmodified gz-sim main (2 of 7 runs). The cause was our harness: the `gz sim` CLI creates the world's models and systems on a background thread unless `--wait-for-assets` is given, so the world stepped empty for a variable number of iterations. With `--wait-for-assets` the toggle test is identical to gz main in 25 of 25 runs on the depth PRs (16a + 16b, 07, 09a, 08, and the stack 16 + 07 + 09a + 08 + 08b; 5 each) and in 5 of 5 on the RGBD one (19).

## Questions for maintainers

0. **Is this split OK?** One change per PR, stacked as listed: 16a/16b after gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391; 07 then 09a; 05 before its users (06, 08, 14, 17, 18); 08b after 08 and 09a.

1. **`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`** (gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (05), details in gazebosim/gz-transport#992).
   Proposal: `bool PublishInPlace(std::size_t _msgSize, const std::function<bool(char *_buffer)> &_serialize)`. The buffer is a Zenoh SHM chunk when the message goes through shared memory, otherwise a heap buffer handed to ZeroMQ or Zenoh. Local subscribers, ordering, throttling and `IgnoreLocalMessages` behave as with `Publish()`. Is a new member on `Publisher` in this shape acceptable?

2. **`Camera::IssueReadback()` and `Sensor::RenderAhead()`** (gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392 (16a), #697 (16b)).
   Proposal: `virtual bool Camera::IssueReadback()`, default false, one name for every camera type (RGB can implement it later). On `Sensor`, a protected virtual `RenderAhead()` (default false, serial), a public `RenderAheadIfDue()` for the Manager, and a protected `RenderedAhead()`. Both add virtuals, so this is an ABI break: main only, and gz-sim must be rebuilt. One order change: a listener attached directly to a rendering camera's frame events runs after the whole run has rendered, not between cameras. The sensors' own callbacks are not affected. Is that OK for main?

3. **Packed xyz point cloud format** (gazebosim/gz-rendering#1394 (09a), **08b**).
   Proposal: `DepthCamera::SetPointCloudFormat(PixelFormat)` with `PF_FLOAT32_RGBA` (default) or `PF_FLOAT32_RGB`. Should it be a pixel format or a boolean "xyz only"? Should `DepthCameraSensor` ask for it for every cloud (08b)? The published messages don't change, but a listener connected directly to `DepthCamera()->ConnectNewRgbPointCloud()` then gets three floats per point instead of four. Or should the sensor ask for it only when configured to?

**Opt-in behaviours.** These change the output, so they would be off by default. I'm asking about each one separately.

4. **16-bit millimetre depth** (09b, branch prepared, no tests yet).
   `<image><format>L_INT16</format>` gives `uint16` depth in mm, as real 16UC1 cameras do (REP 118): 0 means invalid, values are rounded to the nearest mm, and the GPU does the conversion (`DepthCamera::SetDepthImageFormat(PF_L16)`). On the prototype stack, depth image only: 0.083 → 0.065 CPU s per sim s (not measured alone on the current branch). Should the 16-bit frame go through the existing `newDepthFrame` event (a format string, with the `const float *` pointing at `uint16_t` data, as in the prototype), or through a typed `ConnectNewDepthFrame16` like the thermal camera's?

5. **xyz-only point clouds** (09d, branch prepared, no tests yet).
   This drops the grayscale `rgb` field (`point_step` 16 → 12). Most consumers (SLAM, costmaps) ignore it. Prototype stack, `/points` over Zenoh: 0.150 / 6.37 → 0.107 / 9.95 (CPU s per sim s / sim s per wall s). Do you want this option?

6. **Deferred readback** (09c; no PR, asked only as an opt-in question).
   `PostRender()` maps the readback of frame N−1, which the GPU has finished, instead of waiting for frame N. The stamp stays the render time, but the data arrives one sensor period late in sim time, and the first update publishes nothing. That rules it out for closed-loop perception; it could suit datasets, stamp-aligned SLAM and RL. Its case is `/points` wall speed: 6.37 → 9.24 sim s per wall s (+45%) on the prototype stack. With gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 it gives nothing for depth images alone. Render ahead (16) closes most of the gap without any delay: in another batch on the same prototype stack, 5.64 → 7.44 against 7.58 with deferred readback (93% of the gap). Is there interest in this as an opt-in, or should it stay out?

7. **Where should the switches live** (for 4 to 6, and 3 if it becomes opt-in)? An SDF element (for example under `<depth_camera>`, which needs a matching sdformat PR), or a `Sensors` system parameter / sensor API? 16-bit depth can use the existing `<image><format>`.

## Pre-existing bugs found along the way

I can file these separately:

- gz-sensors: `DepthCameraSensor::SetScene()` keeps the point cloud connection on the old camera, and so does `RgbdCameraSensor`. After a scene change, main keeps republishing the last cloud (and, for RGBD, the last image) with new stamps.
- gz-sensors: a sensor that removes itself from its own callback is a use-after-free in `Sensor::Update()`, because the callback runs inside the sensor's method.
- gz-rendering (ogre2): destroying a depth camera while its scene stays alive, then creating another one, trips Ogre's `HlmsDatablock` assertion ("still being used by some Renderables"), the same assertion as gazebosim/gz-sensors#548 (closed; the fix was planned in gz-rendering). Removing an `RgbdCameraSensor` from its `Manager` while the scene lives does the same. It happens on main, with the packaged OgreNext as well.
- Already fixed in this series: an out-of-bounds write in `Lidar` for `<resolution>` > 1 (#691 (01)), and a data race in `Lidar::ApplyNoise`, which wrote the buffer without `lidarMutex` (#693 (06)).

## Additional context

- Zenoh can fall back from shared memory without any message: gazebosim/gz-transport#991.
- ros_gz_bridge maps `L_INT16` to `mono16`. depth_image_proc accepts that, and a small ros_gz change could add `16UC1`.
- Related PRs that change no API: gz-sensors lidar #691 (01), #692 (02); gz-rendering RGB readback gazebosim/gz-rendering#1395 (12), gazebosim/gz-rendering#1396 (13); OgreNext ForwardClustered **15**.

title: Lidar: read the sensor parameters once per scan
body:
# 🎉 New feature

## Summary

`Lidar::PublishLidarScan` fills the `LaserScan` with a loop that, for every range, calls `RangeCount()`, `VerticalRangeCount()`, `RangeMin()` and `RangeMax()` (through `Clamp()`), each going through `sdf::Lidar`, and sets the range and the intensity through the repeated field's setters. On a 2048x128 GPU lidar at 10 Hz that is 26 ms of CPU per simulated second, the largest single item in the profile of the sensor (total 0.128 CPU s per sim s).

This PR reads the parameters once per scan, clamps with the same double precision function (`Clamp()` now calls it), and writes the two arrays through their data pointers.

It also adds `GpuLidarSensorTest.BitExactOutput`, which pins down the published bytes so that this and the following lidar changes can be reviewed as "same bytes", and `Lidar_TEST.PublishMoreRangesThanRays` for the bound below.

The published bytes do not change. One case differs, and only because it wrote out of bounds: when the range count times the vertical range count exceeds the ray count (`<resolution>` > 1), the old loop wrote past the end of the repeated fields. The loop now stops at the message size.

## Behaviour: byte-identical

- `BitExactOutput` overwrites the laser buffer from the `ConnectNewLidarFrame` callback and compares the serialized `LaserScan` and `PointCloudPacked` messages, byte for byte, with messages built independently: metadata from the configured sensor (frame, pose, angles, counts, range limits, the point fields), the requested time and the expected sequence numbers; payload from verbatim copies of the original `Lidar::Clamp` loop and `GpuLidarSensor::FillPointCloudMsg`. Cases: a 641x13 sensor with NaN, +-inf, zero, values on and beyond both range clamps and NaN intensities, a non-dense frame (first invalid ray 16) and a dense one; a 257x1 sensor; Gaussian noise with a fixed seed (301x7), where most in-range values must differ from the injected ones.
- End to end, on the quadruped bench (gz-sim main + this change alone): `/scan` and `/points` compared by CRC of the raw message, matched by stamp, against unmodified gz-sim main, on 3 lidar worlds (static, moving, Gaussian noise with `--seed 7`), both clamps hit, +-inf in view: all identical.

## Test it

```
ctest -R "INTEGRATION_gpu_lidar_sensor"
```

```
ctest -R "UNIT_Lidar_TEST|INTEGRATION_cpu_lidar_sensor"
```

- `BitExactOutput` fails on each mutation of the code under test I tried: NaN clamped to the minimum (on this branch), and, on the development branch with the same test, swapping the order of a product, clamping in float instead of double, a wrong `is_dense`, float ranges, a wrong scan `frame_id`, a constant `seq`, a cloud stamp off by 1 ms, a missing `ApplyNoise`. It needs a GPU (ogre2), like the other tests in that file.
- `Lidar_TEST.PublishMoreRangesThanRays`: 4 rays at resolution 4 (16 ranges); the scan must hold 4 ranges, the first ones. On main the loop writes 16 entries into the 4-entry fields: AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow in `PublishLidarScan`. Without a sanitizer main usually passes it (the write lands in the heap unnoticed).

## Measurements

Quadruped bench: ANYmal on MuJoCo, 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL, gz-sim main (origin/main of gz-sim, gz-sensors, gz-rendering, gz-transport, 2026-10-25). One lidar, `/scan` and `/points` both subscribed: 2048x128 at 10 Hz (S2L2) and 1024x64 at 10 Hz (S2L). CPU: the server's CPU seconds per simulated second, RTF 0, pinned to 1 core. Wall: simulated seconds per wall second, RTF 0, 3 cores. n=5 runs of 20 s per arm, arms interleaved in one batch; mean ± 95% CI (t), and the change with its 95% CI (Welch).

This PR alone, against gz main:

| | transport | gz main | with this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S2L2 CPU, 1 core | ZeroMQ | 0.1258 ± 0.0035 | 0.1025 ± 0.0023 | **-18.6 ± 2.6%** |
| S2L2 CPU, 1 core | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 0.1181 ± 0.0026 | 0.0907 ± 0.0009 | **-23.2 ± 1.8%** |
| S2L2 wall, 3 cores | ZeroMQ | 9.97 ± 0.41 | 12.58 ± 0.52 | **+26.1 ± 6.3%** |
| S2L2 wall, 3 cores | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 10.86 ± 0.73 | 12.78 ± 1.07 | +17.7 ± 10.8% |
| S2L CPU, 1 core | ZeroMQ | 0.0752 ± 0.0013 | 0.0663 ± 0.0038 | -11.9 ± 5.3% |
| S2L CPU, 1 core | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 0.0745 ± 0.0012 | 0.0672 ± 0.0022 | -9.7 ± 2.9% |
| S2L wall, 3 cores | ZeroMQ | 19.59 ± 1.34 | 19.12 ± 1.74 | -2.4 ± 9.5% (none resolved) |
| S2L wall, 3 cores | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 15.61 ± 0.92 | 17.67 ± 1.62 | +13.2 ± 10.9% |

The 3-core runs are noisier than the 1-core ones (the GPU and the sink share the machine).

## Not changing here

- The `\todo(iche033)` about interpolating when the ray count differs from the range count.
- The double copy of the scan (`GpuRays::Data()` is persistent and `laserBuffer` is mutated by the noise and read by `Ranges()`; the API needs both).

## Backport Policy
- [ ] This is safe to backport to the following versions:
    - [ ] Jetty
    - [ ] Ionic
    - [ ] Harmonic
    - [ ] Fortress
- [ ] This **should not** be backported
- [ ] I am not sure
- [x] Other (fill in yourself)

A backport to Jetty may be useful for the out-of-bounds write with `resolution > 1`, which exists in released versions; maintainers to decide. The rest is a performance change.

title: GpuLidarSensor: take the cosine and sine of each azimuth and inclination once per scan
body:
# 🎉 New feature

> Stacked on #691. Until that merges, the diff here also shows the commits below it; this PR is the last commit.

## Summary

`GpuLidarSensor::FillPointCloudMsg` takes the cosine and sine of the row's inclination and the column's azimuth for every point (`sincosf` twice per point), and looks up the field offsets and the point step in the message for every point. Every row sweeps the same azimuths. For a 2048x128 lidar that is 262144 points per scan, and the function is 11 ms of CPU per simulated second at 10 Hz.

This PR computes the azimuths' cosines and sines once per scan (accumulated in float exactly as before), the inclinations' once per row, and hoists the field offsets and the point step out of the loop. The products keep their order and their float precision.

## Behaviour: byte-identical

The point cloud bytes are unchanged. `GpuLidarSensorTest.BitExactOutput` (added by PR 01) compares the serialized `PointCloudPacked` with a verbatim copy of the original `FillPointCloudMsg`, including NaN, +-inf, zero and out-of-range values and a non-dense frame. The `/points` topic was also compared by raw message CRC against unmodified gz-sim main on the bench (gz-sim main + PRs 01 and 02), matched by stamp: identical on 3 lidar worlds (static, moving, noise with `--seed 7`).

## Test it

```
ctest -R "INTEGRATION_gpu_lidar_sensor"
```

`BitExactOutput` fails when the x product is reassociated (`depth * (cosInclination * cos(azimuth))`), and on the other mutations listed in PR 01 (product order, `is_dense`, ...).

## Measurements

# 🎉 New feature

> Stacked on #692. Until that merges, the diff here also shows the commits below it; this PR is the last 2 commits.

Part of #690. Needs gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`).

## Summary

The LaserScan and the point cloud of a GPU lidar are built in a protobuf message and then copied again by `Publish()` when it serializes them. For a 2048x128 lidar that is 262144 points (4.7 MB per point cloud) per scan, written twice.

This PR serializes both messages straight into the transport's buffer with `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`:

- `Lidar`: the LaserScan's `ranges` and `intensities` (its last two fields) are written as packed doubles after the rest of `laserMsg`, which no longer holds them.
- `GpuLidarSensor`: the point cloud's `data` is written between the fields before it and `is_dense`, which is found first (a pre-scan of the laser buffer). `pointMsg` no longer holds `data`.
- The density pre-scan and the point fill run under `lidarMutex`, so `is_dense` and the points always describe one frame. The subscriber callbacks run on the publish thread (gz-transport), so holding the lock while publishing is safe, as `PublishLidarScan` always did.
- When there are fewer ranges than rays (`<resolution>` below 1), gz-sensors writes only the first `RangeCount() x VerticalRangeCount()` entries and the rest keep the values of earlier scans (NaN at first, reset when the ray count changes). That case keeps the original message path (update `laserMsg`, `Publish`), so it stays as before.
- `Lidar::ApplyNoise` now writes the laser buffer under `lidarMutex`. `Range()` and `Ranges()` read it under that lock, possibly from a subscriber callback on another thread; the noise write was unlocked (a data race on main).

The point cloud's in-place encoding (fields before, data tag and length, data, fields after) goes through `PublishWithData` in the internal header `src/PublishInPlace.hh` (not installed). #693/#694/#695/#699 add the same file byte for byte (#696 gets it from #695), so they merge in any order. The scan writes its two packed fields with the same `CodedOutputStream` calls.

## Behaviour: byte-identical

- `GpuLidarSensorTest.BitExactOutput` builds the expected `LaserScan` and `PointCloudPacked` independently of the received messages (metadata from the configured sensor, the requested times and the expected sequence numbers: scan 2f, cloud 2f+1; payload from verbatim copies of the original routines) and compares byte for byte. Cases: a 641x13 sensor with NaN, +-inf, zero and values on and beyond both clamps, a dense and a non-dense frame (first invalid ray 16), a 257x1 sensor, and Gaussian noise with a fixed seed (301x7) where most in-range values must differ from the injected ones.
- End to end on the quadruped bench: `/scan` and `/points` compared by raw message CRC against unmodified gz-sim main, matched by stamp, on 3 lidar worlds x 4 topics, over ZeroMQ and Zenoh SHM 64 MiB: all identical (static, moving and noise worlds with `--seed 7`, both clamps hit, +-inf).
- Differences, all in corners:
  - writes are bounded by the message size, which fixes an out-of-bounds write on main when `resolution > 1` (PR 01);
  - a reload of the *same* `Lidar` object from resolution 1 to below 1 at the same ray count leaves a NaN tail, not the last resolution-1 scan. Matching main would cost a copy of every scan, and gz-sim never reloads a sensor object;
  - the template messages are private and have no unknown fields; if one ever did, the in-place layout would put it before the payload instead of after the known fields (a comment says so);

## Test it

```
ctest -R "INTEGRATION_gpu_lidar_sensor|UNIT_Lidar_TEST"
```

- `GpuLidarSensorTest.BitExactOutput` (from PR 01): builds the expected messages independently and compares byte for byte; the mutations it catches are listed in PR 01.
- `Lidar_TEST.PublishedTailKeepsEarlierScans`: 4 rays at resolution 0.75, then a reload at 0.5, then 1. The tail of the ranges keeps the previous scan's values. It fails with the first version of the in-place encoder (NaN tail).
- `Lidar_TEST.PublishMoreRangesThanRays` (PR 01) also runs the in-place path (resolution > 1: one range per ray).
- Not tested: the two locking changes (the density pre-scan and fill under `lidarMutex`, and `ApplyNoise`) have no ThreadSanitizer test; the review argued them by reading.

## Measurements

Quadruped bench: ANYmal on MuJoCo, 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL, gz-sim main (origin/main of gz-sim, gz-sensors, gz-rendering, gz-transport, 2026-10-25). One lidar, `/scan` and `/points` both subscribed: 2048x128 at 10 Hz (S2L2) and 1024x64 at 10 Hz (S2L). CPU: the server's CPU seconds per simulated second, RTF 0, pinned to 1 core. Wall: simulated seconds per wall second, RTF 0, 3 cores. n=5 runs of 20 s per arm, arms interleaved in one batch; the base is gz main + PRs 01, 02 and 05; mean ± 95% CI (t), and the change with its 95% CI (Welch).

This PR alone, against PRs 01 + 02 + 05:

| | transport | base | base + this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S2L2 CPU, 1 core | ZeroMQ | 0.0958 ± 0.0057 | 0.0894 ± 0.0023 | -6.6 ± 5.6% |
| S2L2 CPU, 1 core | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 0.0852 ± 0.0010 | 0.0793 ± 0.0007 | **-6.9 ± 1.2%** |
| S2L2 wall, 3 cores | ZeroMQ | 14.27 ± 1.38 | 14.21 ± 0.15 | -0.4 ± 9.6% (not resolved) |
| S2L2 wall, 3 cores | Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 14.32 ± 2.22 | 14.20 ± 0.60 | -0.8 ± 16.0% (not resolved) |
| S2L CPU, 1 core | ZeroMQ | 0.0647 ± 0.0036 | 0.0627 ± 0.0029 | -3.1 ± 6.0% (not resolved) |

# 🎉 New feature

Part of #690. Needs gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`).

## Summary

When the image is only published (no image callback, no saving), `CameraSensor::Update` copies the frame into `imageMsg.data`, and then `Publish()` serializes the message, copying the frame again into the serialization buffer.

This PR publishes it with `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace` instead: the fields before the data (header, width, height, step) and after it (`pixel_format_type`) are serialized around the frame, which the camera copies once, straight into the transport's buffer. With an image callback or image saving, the copying path is unchanged.

The in-place encoding (fields before, data tag and length, data, fields after) goes through `PublishWithData` in the internal header `src/PublishInPlace.hh` (not installed). #693/#694/#695/#699 add the same file byte for byte (#696 gets it from #695), so they merge in any order.
