# 🎉 New feature

Part of #690. Needs gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`).

## Summary

`OnNewDepthFrame` copies every depth frame into `depthBuffer`, `Update` copies it again into the message (`set_data`), and `Publish()` serializes it, a third full-frame copy.

This PR publishes the depth image from `OnNewDepthFrame` itself, while `Update` renders, with `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`: the fields before the data (header, width, height, step) and after it (`pixel_format_type`) are serialized around the frame, which is written once, from the readback straight into the transport's buffer. Only a depth clip (`<depth_camera><clip>`) still copies the frame into `depthBuffer`, where the clip is applied as before and the point cloud reads it.

The in-place encoding (fields before, data tag and length, data, fields after) goes through `PublishWithData` in the internal header `src/PublishInPlace.hh` (not installed). #693/#694/#695/#699 add the same file byte for byte (#696 gets it from #695), so they merge in any order.

Compared by raw CRC per message, matched by stamp, with gz-sim main on gz-rendering main: image, depth image and point cloud of three RGBD cameras (320x240, 640x480, 161x121 with a depth clip), on a static, a moving, a noise (`--seed 7`) and a point-light-transition world, plus a subscriber toggle (depth throughout, image and points subscribed and dropped twice), over ZeroMQ and Zenoh: all identical (every topic, every world, both transports).

title: RgbdCameraSensor: publish the point cloud and image in place
body:
# 🎉 New feature

> Stacked on #695. Until that merges, the diff here also shows the commits below it; this PR is the last commit.

Follows #695. Needs gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`).

## Summary

For every frame with point cloud or image subscribers, `OnNewRgbPointCloud` copies the RGBA point cloud (16 bytes per pixel, 4.9 MB at 640x480) into `pointCloudBuffer`. `Update` then fills the point cloud message and an RGB image from it with `PointCloudUtil` (per point, a protobuf lookup of each field's offset and an out-of-line colour decode), copies the image into its message (`set_data`), and `Publish()` serializes both messages, copying each again.

This PR publishes both from `OnNewRgbPointCloud`, while `Update` renders, with `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`. Each is written once, from the readback straight into the transport's buffer: the points as x, y, z and the colour bytes b, g, r, 0 (the layout `CreateCameras` gives the message), the image as r, g, b. The fields around the data are serialized as before. `is_dense` follows the data in the message, so the cloud is written with the last cloud's value and written again only when it changed. With a depth clip, points whose clipped depth is +-inf take it as x, y and z, as before.

## Behaviour: byte-identical, three differences

The bytes are those `Publish()` sent. Same equivalence set as #695 (image, depth image and point cloud of three RGBD cameras on four worlds plus a subscriber toggle, raw CRC per message matched by stamp against gz-sim main, ZeroMQ and Zenoh): all identical.

Differences, all on error paths:
- a frame the depth camera fails to deliver is not published (`Update` published the previous cloud and image again with a new stamp and sequence number);
- a point cloud frame with other than 4 channels is dropped with an error (`Update` read it as 4 channels);
- a point cloud frame whose size differs from the message's publishes the image only, with an error (`Update` filled the message from it regardless).

Known, pre-existing: `SetScene()` leaves the point cloud connection on the old camera, so after a scene change `Update` kept publishing the last cloud and image; now it publishes neither. A fix belongs in `SetScene()`.

## Test it

```
ctest -R INTEGRATION_rgbd_camera
```

`PublishedBytesMatchCopy` (#695) covers the point cloud and image too. It fails when the cloud's colour bytes are swapped, when is_dense is not rewritten, when the clip does not override xyz, or when the image's channel order is wrong.

## Measurements

Quadruped bench as in #695 (S2R6: six 640x480 RGBD cameras at 15 Hz with a sun). CPU s per sim s on 1 core, sim s per wall s on 3 cores, RTF 0, n=5, 20 s, mean ± 95% CI, interleaved with the base (gz main + gazebosim/gz-transport#993 + #695):

| subscribers | CPU s/sim s, 1 core: base | + this PR | Δ | sim s/wall s, 3 cores: base | + this PR | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| image only | 0.4404 ± 0.0242 | 0.2954 ± 0.0298 | **−32.9% ± 8.7** | 3.28 ± 0.14 | 3.94 ± 0.11 | **+20.1% ± 5.4** |
| image + depth image + points | 0.7535 ± 0.0445 | 0.5902 ± 0.0270 | **−21.7% ± 6.9** | 1.76 ± 0.07 | 2.42 ± 0.48 | +37.8% ± 27.9 |
| depth image only (unchanged path) | 0.1807 ± 0.0097 | 0.1768 ± 0.0096 | −2.2% ± 7.6 | 7.06 ± 0.26 | 6.92 ± 0.43 | −2.0% ± 7.1 |

Image only: −33% CPU, +20% wall; all topics: −22% CPU, about +38% wall (one slow 3-core run widens that CI). The depth-only row is a control (unchanged path).

title: Manager: render ahead, so depth camera and GPU lidar readbacks overlap
body:
# 🎉 New feature

## Summary

`Manager::RunOnce` updates the sensors one after another. For a depth camera or a GPU lidar, `Update()` renders, then waits for the GPU-to-CPU transfer of its output, then publishes. With several such sensors the transfer latencies add up on the render thread: with six 640x480 depth cameras on gz-sim, physics waits for rendering 61% of the wall time.

This PR updates in two passes. A run of consecutive sensors that can render ahead first all render and issue their GPU readbacks (`rendering::Camera::IssueReadback()`, gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392); then each `Update()` waits for its own readback and publishes. Any other sensor completes the pending run before its own `Update()`, so GPU commands and random draws keep the serial order.

- `Sensor`: `RenderAheadIfDue()` (public, for the Manager) applies `Update()`'s due checks without consuming a trigger (triggered sensors never render ahead), and calls the protected virtual `RenderAhead()` (default false: serial). The protected `RenderedAhead()` tells `Update(_now)` that it completes such a frame; it is valid only until the end of the next `Update(_now, _force)`, so a frame whose update was skipped is never completed later.
- `DepthCameraSensor` and `GpuLidarSensor` render ahead when `Update()` would render only the camera (manual scene update) and no user code runs between the serial renders: no image or lidar frame callbacks, no CPU lidar noise (it draws random numbers in `Update()`). A frame rendered ahead is completed by the next `Update()` only; `SetScene()` drops it. Only these exact types render ahead: a subclass renders serially, because its override of `Update()` must run before its frame renders.
- `Update()` callbacks may remove or add sensors: `RunOnce` looks sensors up by id again after every call that may run them, and visits sensors added after the last run as the serial loop does.

## Behaviour: same messages; one documented change of order

The published messages (data, stamps, sequence numbers) are the same as without this PR.

What changes:
- **Frame events fire after the whole run has rendered.** A listener attached directly to a rendering camera's events (`DepthCamera()->ConnectNewDepthFrame()`, `GpuRays()->ConnectNewGpuRaysFrame()`) now runs after the other cameras of the run rendered, not between them. The sensors' own callbacks (`ConnectImageCallback`, lidar frame callbacks) keep the sensor serial, so they are not affected. gz-sim and gz-sensors attach no other listener; a user listener that draws random numbers or edits the scene would see a different order.
- **Subscribers that connect or leave between the two passes:** the frame rendered ahead is completed as `RenderAhead()` saw them, as if they had changed just after this update (the serial path has the same race at another instant). A depth camera now publishes a point cloud only for a frame rendered with the cloud connected; on main, a cloud subscriber connecting at the wrong instant could get the previous frame's cloud with a new stamp.
- With the legacy readback (`IssueReadback()` returns false), `PostRender()` still downloads, after the other cameras' draws, from each camera's own texture: same data.

## ABI

Adds virtuals to `gz::sensors::Sensor`: ABI change, so `main` only; gz-sim (and anything deriving from `Sensor`) must be rebuilt.

## Test it

```
ctest -R "UNIT_Manager_TEST|INTEGRATION_depth_camera|INTEGRATION_gpu_lidar_sensor"
```

`Manager_TEST.RenderAheadOrder`: six fake sensors (render-ahead, serial, not due) check the run order (`RA RB UA* UB* UC RD UD* UF`, `*` = `Update()` saw `RenderedAhead()`), a callback that removes a pending sensor and the current one, a sensor added by a callback of the last run (updated in the same `RunOnce`), and a deactivated pending sensor whose later forced update must not complete the abandoned frame. Five perturbations each fail it (two by segfault): the pointer loop instead of ids, no due check in `RenderAheadIfDue`, no re-lookup of the current sensor, no resume after the last run, no clearing of the rendered-ahead state.

`DepthCameraSensorTest.RenderAheadOnlyExactType` and `GpuLidarSensorTest.RenderAheadOnlyExactType` (ogre2): a trivial subclass of the sensor does not render ahead where the sensor itself does; without the exact-type check both fail.

Not covered by a unit test: the depth camera cloud gate and the lidar noise/callback gating (covered end to end below: the toggle world and the noise world).

## Equivalence (end to end)

gz-sim main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + this pair vs gz-sim main, every message's raw bytes compared by CRC, matched by stamp, over ZeroMQ:
- depth: 4 worlds (static, moving, 16 moving boxes, 16 spawned boxes), 3 depth cameras each, depth images and point clouds: identical (spawn16: the first frame's stamp differs in one run, a known sink start-up race).
- lidar: static, moving, Gaussian noise (`--seed 7`; noisy lidars stay serial): identical.
- toggle world (subscribers connect and leave, a mover crosses the view): identical to gz main in 5 of 5 runs with this PR (16a + 16b; depth images and point clouds of the three cameras, headers included; fixed harness). The earlier runs, in which the forward camera (the one the mover crosses) differed from the mover's entry in 4 of 5 runs with this PR and in 2 of 7 on unmodified gz main, each with its own bytes, came from our harness stepping the world before gz-sim had created the entities. The `gz sim` CLI creates the world's models and systems on a background thread unless `--wait-for-assets`, so the world stepped empty for a variable number of iterations and the mover's whole trajectory shifted by that many steps. This PR neither caused nor cured it; it only changed how often the bench's first step won that race.

## Measurements

Quadruped bench: ANYmal on MuJoCo, 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL, gz-sim main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 with and without this pair (gz-sim rebuilt), ZeroMQ, 20 s runs, arms interleaved, mean ± 95% CI. Wall: simulated seconds per wall second on 3 cores at RTF 0. CPU: server CPU seconds per simulated second on 1 core.

| scenario | wall, 3 cores (n=5) | Δ | CPU, 1 core (n=5) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| six 640x480 depth cameras @15 Hz, depth images | 5.74 ± 0.30 -> 7.96 ± 1.18 | **+39%** | 0.1650 ± 0.0092 -> 0.1536 ± 0.0044 | -6.9% |
| same, depth + `/points` | 1.64 ± 0.22 -> 2.30 ± 0.36 | **+40%** | 0.5153 ± 0.0048 -> 0.4683 ± 0.0060 | **-9.1%** |
| three 2048x128 GPU lidars @10 Hz | 4.28 ± 0.24 -> 4.82 ± 0.34 | **+13%** | 0.2599 ± 0.0022 -> 0.2565 ± 0.0079 | -1.3% (noise) |
| one 2048x128 GPU lidar | 9.9 -> 10.6 (n=2) | noise | 0.122 -> 0.120 (n=2) | noise |

CPU does not rise: on one core the overlapped transfers replace the serial waits (the depth rows drop by 7 to 9%); the lidar row is within noise. One sensor alone cannot gain: a run of one renders and completes back to back. The gain is larger on main than it would be with a depth-only readback, because every depth frame on main reads back the full RGBA float point-cloud texture (4.9 MB per camera), so each serial wait is long.

## Known issues on main, not changed here (follow-ups)

- A sensor that removes itself from its own callback is a use-after-free in `Sensor::Update` (the callback runs inside the sensor's method). This PR does not make it worse: `RunOnce` re-finds the current sensor by id after each call.
- `DepthCameraSensor::SetScene` keeps the old point-cloud connection (the same bug exists in `RgbdCameraSensor`).
- A sensor constructed before the current one but added by a pending sensor's callback is visited in the next `RunOnce` (serial: in this one). Sensor ids come from construction order; gz-sim adds sensors outside `RunOnce`.

title: RgbdCameraSensor: render ahead, so RGBD readbacks overlap

# 🎉 New feature

> Stacked on #697. Until that merges, the diff here also shows the commits below it; this PR is the last commit.

## Summary

#697 lets `Manager::RunOnce` render a run of sensors and issue their GPU readbacks first, then complete each `Update()`; it enabled this for depth cameras and GPU lidars. This PR does the same for `RgbdCameraSensor`, which renders one `Ogre2DepthCamera` (it already implements `IssueReadback()`, gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392).

- `RenderAhead()`: when the sensor is initialized, uses manual scene update and has an image, depth or points subscriber, connect the point cloud callback as `Update()` would, `Render()`, `IssueReadback()`. Only `RgbdCameraSensor` itself (exact type): a subclass renders in its own `Update()`.
- `Update()`: a frame rendered ahead is completed with `PostRender()` (maps the issued readback, fires the depth and cloud callbacks); otherwise unchanged.
- The colour image and point cloud are published only when the point cloud callback is connected. On main, `Update()` published from the point cloud buffer whenever it existed, so a subscriber connecting between the render and the publish got the previous frame's cloud and image with a new stamp; render-ahead widens that window.
- `SetScene()` drops a frame rendered ahead.

No image callbacks exist on this sensor. Image noise is a render pass that draws its random numbers in the scene's `PreRender()` (before any sensor renders), so noisy sensors render ahead too.

## Behaviour

Same messages (data, stamps, sequence numbers) as without this PR, checked end to end below. Subscribers that connect or leave between the two passes see the frame as `RenderAhead()` saw them (as in 16b); a points/image subscriber that connects between the passes gets its first cloud from the next frame.

Merging with #695/#696: the rendered-ahead `PostRender()` in `RgbdCameraSensor.cc` must also be bracketed by `frameStamp = _now; … reset()` as the serial one is. Without it, frames rendered ahead publish no depth, cloud or image. Whichever lands second has to add it.

## ABI

None (overrides a virtual added by 16b).

## Test it

```
ctest -R "INTEGRATION_rgbd_camera|INTEGRATION_depth_camera|UNIT_Manager_TEST"
```

`RgbdCameraSensorTest.RenderAheadMatchesSerial` (ogre2): two RGBD sensors, a moving box, 4 frames rendered ahead vs serial: depth, image and points byte-identical, and different from the previous frame. A late-subscriber step checks the gate: image and points leave, the sensor renders ahead, points come back before `Update()`: depth is published, the cloud is not. Perturbations: no cloud gate (fails), `Update()` not calling `PostRender()` on a frame rendered ahead (fails).

title: DepthCameraSensor: copy the depth frame once and publish the image and the point cloud in place
body:
# 🎉 New feature

> Stacked on #697. Until that merges, the diff here also shows the commits below it; this PR is the last 2 commits.

Part of #690 (cutting the CPU cost of depth cameras). Needs gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`) and #697 (render ahead).

## Summary

For every depth frame the sensor copied the frame into a buffer, then into the message, then `Publish()` serialized it into the transport's buffer (1.2 MB each at 640x480). The point cloud was worse: the sensor copied the camera's RGBA cloud (16 B per point, 4.9 MB) into a buffer, extracted xyz into another, converted the depth into a grayscale image, filled the message from those, and `Publish()` serialized it.

1. **Copy once** (`c4773d6`). The depth frame is copied once, straight into the message's data, which is reused frame to frame. The point cloud message is filled in one loop from the camera's cloud, inside the callback (the sensor no longer keeps a pointer into the render engine's memory past it): xyz from the first three channels, the grayscale colour from channel 0 (the depth), with the colour scale (the largest finite depth) found while the depth frame is copied. The same loop finds `is_dense`.
2. **Publish in place** (`5205c9b`). Without image callbacks, the depth frame callback publishes the image itself with `PublishInPlace`: the header, width, height and step serialized in field order, then the data tag and length, the frame straight from the render engine's buffer, then the pixel format. The point cloud is published the same way from its callback. `is_dense` follows the data but decides the message size, so the message is serialized with the previous cloud's `is_dense`, the fill finds this one's, and on a change the publication is cancelled and filled again: no pre-scan, and the bytes are those of `Publish(msg)`. The publication moves from the end of `Update()` into the frame callbacks, which run inside the same `Update()` (in `Render()`, or in `PostRender()` for a frame rendered ahead) with the same stamp and sequence number. With an image callback, or for a render outside `Update()`, the cloud is filled into the message and `Update()` publishes the image, runs the callbacks, then publishes the cloud, as before.

The in-place encoding (fields before, data tag and length, data, fields after) goes through `PublishWithData` in the internal header `src/PublishInPlace.hh` (not installed). #693/#694/#695/#699 add the same file byte for byte (#696 gets it from #695), so they merge in any order.

## Behaviour: byte-identical

The bytes on the wire are those of `Publish(msg)` of the messages built as before. Differences in when something is published, both cases where main republished stale data:
- a point cloud is published only for a frame the render engine delivered one for (main republished the last cloud with a new stamp, e.g. in the frame a subscriber connects);
- nothing is published when the render delivered no depth frame (main republished the last one).

End to end (quadruped bench, gz-sim main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + PR 05 + this PR, Zenoh, raw CRC per message matched by stamp against unmodified gz-sim main): depth images and point clouds identical, headers included, in four worlds (static, moving, 16 moving boxes, 16 spawned boxes; three cameras each) and in the toggle test (subscribers connect and leave; 30 of 30 clouds per camera). In 5 of 5 toggle runs with the fixed harness all three cameras are identical to gz-sim main. (Earlier toggle runs differed on the forward camera from t=1.667 on, where a moving model enters its view; that came from our harness stepping the world before gz-sim had created the entities, not from this PR; see #697.)

## Test it

```
ctest -R INTEGRATION_depth_camera
```

`DepthCameraSensorTest.PublishedBytesMatchReference` compares the published depth image and point cloud bytes with `Publish()` of the messages built the original way (a fresh `msgs::Image`; `PointCloudUtil::FillMsg` from the xyz and a grayscale image), with the sensor rendering ahead (manual scene update, as gz-sim), with an image callback (serial path, the cloud after the image), `is_dense` true, false, true, a depth-only frame while the cloud subscriber is away, and the frame in which it comes back (its own cloud, nothing stale). Three perturbations each fail it: the image data written under the wrong field tag, no refill when `is_dense` changes (no cloud arrives), and a colour scale kept from the first frame (wrong grey in later clouds).

## Measurements

Quadruped bench: ANYmal on MuJoCo, 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL, six 640x480 depth cameras at 15 Hz (S2D), RTF 0. CPU: server CPU seconds per simulated second on 1 core; wall: simulated seconds per wall second on 3 cores. n=5 × 20 s per arm, arms interleaved, mean ± 95% CI. Base: gz-sim main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + PR 05; this PR alone on top.

| S2D | CPU, 1 core | Δ | wall, 3 cores | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| depth images only | 0.1575 ± 0.0055 -> 0.1379 ± 0.0073 | **-12.4%** | 8.81 ± 0.73 -> 10.99 ± 1.18 | **+25%** |
| + `/points`, ZeroMQ | 0.4786 ± 0.0090 -> 0.3199 ± 0.0099 | **-33.2%** | 2.57 ± 0.03 -> 3.85 ± 0.19 | **+50%** |
| + `/points`, Zenoh SHM 64 MiB | 0.4134 ± 0.0078 -> 0.2557 ± 0.0071 | **-38.1%** | 2.53 ± 0.08 -> 4.25 ± 0.38 | **+68%** |

## Known limits

- The in-place paths write little-endian protobuf wire data (the platforms gz-sensors supports).
- The `rgb` channel of the cloud is still the grayscale of the depth, computed on the CPU (unchanged).
- Known, pre-existing: `DepthCameraSensor::SetScene()` keeps the point-cloud connection on the old camera (see #697). On main, `Update()` then kept republishing the last cloud with new stamps; here a cloud is published only for a frame the render engine delivered, so after a scene change none is. A fix belongs in `SetScene()`.
- Whether the image is published in place is decided at the start of `Update()`: in place when `ConnectImageCallback` has no listeners. This concerns only C++ listeners of `DepthCameraSensor::ConnectImageCallback()`; **transport subscribers are not affected**: they do not enter this decision. Whether an update renders and publishes is decided as on main (and by 16b for frames rendered ahead), and in place or not the bytes are those of `Publish()`, so a topic subscriber that connects between the passes gets the same first image as on main (checked end to end by the toggle test). An image callback connected *during* an update (after it started, before it ended) is called from the next update; on main it was called in the same one. Who can do that: (a) user code attached directly to the rendering camera (`DepthCamera()->ConnectNewDepthFrame()` or the cloud event) that calls `ConnectImageCallback()` from inside that listener: deterministic on main, one update later here; such a listener always runs after the sensor's own frame callback (connected at load), so deciding at frame time instead would not help; (b) another thread connecting mid-update: already a race on main (main checks the listener count after publishing). Nothing in gz-sim or gz-sensors does either. Calling it in the same update would need a copy of the frame kept until the end of `Update()`, the 1.2 MB copy per frame this PR removes; not done.

Depends on https://github.com/gazebosim/gz-rendering/pull/1418

Forward `<camera><depth_camera><clip><near>` and `<far>` to `gz::rendering::DepthCamera::SetDepthNearClipPlane` and `SetDepthFarClipPlane` in `DepthCameraSensor` and `RgbdCameraSensor`.

title: WideAngleCameraSensor: publish camera_info that matches the lens
body:
# 🦟 Bug fix

Fixes #592

## Summary

`WideAngleCameraSensor` filled its `CameraInfo` message through the regular pinhole path (`PopulateInfo` with the SDF `<lens><intrinsics>`). Those intrinsics don't describe the wide angle lens, so the published message always said `plumb_bob` and gave a focal length unrelated to the rendered image.

This PR derives the camera info from the lens instead:

- **Focal length** comes from the lens mapping `r = c1 * f * fun(theta / c2 + c3)`, where `r` is in units of half the image width. The focal length in pixels is the slope at `theta = 0`: `width / 2 * c1 * f / c2`. When `scale_to_hfov` is set, `f` is first solved so that `hfov / 2` maps to the image edge, the same way the renderer does.
- **Principal point** is the image center.
- **Distortion model**: `equidistant` for equidistant lenses (the model is exact), `plumb_bob` for everything else, both with zero coefficients. The wide angle camera doesn't apply `<distortion>`, so zeros are correct. For gnomonical lenses this is an exact pinhole. Stereographic, equisolid, orthographic and custom lenses have no exact match among the `CameraInfo` models, so they keep `plumb_bob` with the correct focal length and center.
- A small protected helper, `CameraSensor::SetInfoDistortion`, sets the model and coefficients after `PopulateInfo`. It's a non-virtual addition, so the ABI stays compatible.

### Limitations

- The focal-length formula assumes `c3 = 0`. That holds for every built-in lens type; only a custom lens with an angle offset breaks it.
- For lens types other than equidistant and gnomonical, the published model is an approximation (the correct focal length at the center, but no distortion term). I can add a closer fit for those if you'd like, but there is no model in `msgs::CameraInfo` that represents them exactly.

## Test it

New `CameraInfoMatchesLens` test in `test/integration/wide_angle_camera.cc`:
- An equidistant lens with `hfov = 2.2689` at 400x300 must publish `equidistant`, 4 zero coefficients, `fx = fy = 400 / hfov`, and `cx, cy = 200, 150` in both K and P.
- A gnomonical lens with `hfov = pi / 2` must publish `plumb_bob`, 5 zero coefficients, and `fx = fy = 200 / tan(hfov / 2)`.

Ran locally on Ubuntu 24.04 (WSL2, WSLg) with conda-forge Jetty dependencies and the ogre2 render engine:

```
$ ./bin/INTEGRATION_wide_angle_camera
[       OK ] WideAngleCameraSensor/WideAngleCameraSensorTest.ImagesWithBuiltinSDF/ogre2
[       OK ] WideAngleCameraSensor/WideAngleCameraSensorTest.CustomCameraInfoTopic/ogre2
[       OK ] WideAngleCameraSensor/WideAngleCameraSensorTest.CameraInfoMatchesLens/ogre2
[  PASSED  ] 3 tests.

$ ./bin/INTEGRATION_camera
[  PASSED  ] 5 tests.

# With src/WideAngleCameraSensor.cc reverted to main, the new test fails:
Expected equality of these values: ... Which is: 2 / Which is: 0   (model: equidistant vs plumb_bob)
[  FAILED  ] WideAngleCameraSensor/WideAngleCameraSensorTest.CameraInfoMatchesLens/ogre2
```

title: Marine Radar for Gazebo
body:
## Desired behavior
Add a simulated marine radar sensor for Gazebo Harmonic with ROS 2 support, designed to be mounted on a USV (unmanned surface vehicle). Most Gazebo sensor setups are built around land and aerial robots, so marine-specific sensors such as radar are largely missing. A radar plugin that publishes standard ROS 2 messages would let users test USV perception, collision avoidance, and sensor fusion in simulation without hardware.

The sensor should expose configurable parameters for:
- Maximum range, beam geometry, and update rate
- Noise and clutter assumptions
- Mounting pose on the vessel

## Alternatives considered
- Using existing LiDAR or camera sensors as stand-ins for radar. These do not reproduce radar's range, resolution, or noise characteristics.
- Writing one-off radar models inside individual projects. This duplicates effort and does not give the community a shared, documented implementation.
- Reusing marine simulation packages such as Stonefish or the UUV Simulator. I have not yet confirmed whether they provide a radar sensor, so this comparison is still open.

## Implementation suggestion
- Implement as a Gazebo sensor plugin that publishes ROS 2 messages.
- Document the model's range, beam, noise, and clutter parameters so users can judge whether it fits their use case.
- Provide a sample world, launch file, and a short README showing a radar mounted on a USV.
- Release under a permissive license.
- If possible, validate the simulated output against a small recording from a real radar.

## Additional context
I am developing this as part of my own work and would welcome feedback on the model design and on whether it would be useful to others.

title: Add marine radar as a native gz-sensors component
body:
## Summary

Integrates a marine radar simulation as a first-class `MarineRadarSensor`,
built into gz-sensors as a new `marine_radar` component — following the
same `RenderingSensor` + custom-sensor-type pattern already used by
`DopplerVelocityLog`.

The original implementation cast rays through gz-sim's physics ECM, which
gz-sensors cannot depend on. The engine-agnostic scan/echo/target-extraction/
PPI-rendering core is vendored in under `src/marine_radar/` largely
unchanged; only the ray-casting back end is replaced with
`gz::rendering::RayQuery` (as `Lidar`/`GpuLidarSensor` already do), with
surface normals recovered via probe rays since `RayQuery` does not report
them.

Also fixes a pre-existing `sdf::Sensor::FrameId()` build failure against
sdformat 14 in `Sensor.cc` (that API was added in sdformat 15) — gated
behind `SDF_MAJOR_VERSION` with a fallback to the existing
`gz_frame_id`/name lookup.

## Test plan

- [x] `cmake` configure + `make` build the new `marine_radar` component cleanly
- [x] 18/18 new unit + integration tests pass (`UNIT_RadarConfig_TEST`,
      `UNIT_ScanGeometry_TEST`, `UNIT_EchoModel_TEST`,
      `UNIT_TargetExtraction_TEST`, `UNIT_PpiRenderer_TEST`,
      `UNIT_RadarProcessor_TEST`, `UNIT_RadarGzMessages_TEST`,

title: Feature request: pre-publication camera image callback for synchronized pose metadata
body:
## Problem

CameraSensor publishes gz::msgs::Image before invoking
ConnectImageCallback. An external integration that needs to attach
simulation-time pose or hardware timestamp metadata must therefore
subscribe to the already-published image and republish the complete
pixel payload.

This creates two large image deliveries per frame.

## Use case

A camera-pose synchronization plugin associates every rendered image
with the camera's world pose at the image simulation timestamp.

## Measured result

320×240 RGB at 10 FPS:

- Current republish design: 4.6249 MB/s
- External raw-image + pose design: 4.6180 MB/s
- Integrated single-publication estimate: 2.313 MB/s

Both external designs still involve two large publisher-subscriber
delivery pairs.

## Proposed direction

Provide a pre-publication callback or transformation API:

using ImageMutator =
    std::function<void(gz::msgs::Image &)>;

ConnectionPtr ConnectImageMutator(ImageMutator callback);

CameraSensor::Update():
    populate image;
    invoke image mutators;
    publisher.Publish(image);
    invoke ordinary const observers;

The exact API is open for maintainer discussion.

title: Camera: support B8G8R8 image format
body:
# Bug fix

Fixes #543

## Summary

A camera sensor with `<format>B8G8R8</format>` never produced BGR images. `CameraSensor::CreateCamera` maps the SDF pixel format to a gz-rendering format, and that switch had no B8G8R8 case, so it logged `Unsupported pixel format [8]` and the camera stayed on RGB8. The switch in `Update` that picks the `msgs::Image` and `common::Image` format had the same gap. This adds the missing case to both.

The issue mentions 32FC3 on the ROS side. I could not reproduce that with a plain camera sensor. What I saw before the fix was the error above and images published as RGB_INT8.

New test `CameraSensorTest.BGRImagesWithBuiltinSDF` loads a B8G8R8 camera over a pure red background and checks the rendering camera format, the published pixel format, the step, the data size, and that the first pixel is B=0, G=0, R=255.

Built against gz-rendering main (929ecc93) on Ubuntu 24.04 and run under xvfb. Without the fix the new test fails (trimmed):

```
[error] [CameraSensor.cc:249] Unsupported pixel format [8]
test/integration/camera.cc:956: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  gz::rendering::PF_B8G8R8
    Which is: 3
  sensor->RenderingCamera()->ImageFormat()
    Which is: 2
test/integration/camera.cc:983: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  gz::msgs::PixelFormatType::BGR_INT8
    Which is: 8
  g_bgrImage.pixel_format_type()
    Which is: 3
[  FAILED  ] CameraSensor/CameraSensorTest.BGRImagesWithBuiltinSDF/ogre2
```

With the fix `INTEGRATION_camera` passes 6/6 on ogre2, and the new test also passes on ogre. `UNIT_Camera_TEST`, `INTEGRATION_triggered_camera` and `INTEGRATION_wide_angle_camera` pass. I did not run the rest of the suite. `INTEGRATION_depth_camera` (depth_camera.cc:383, inf vs -inf) and `INTEGRATION_rgbd_camera` (rgbd_camera.cc:591, same mismatch) fail in my xvfb setup, and they fail the same way on unmodified main.

The commit cherry-picks cleanly onto gz-sensors10, gz-sensors9 and gz-sensors8 (not built there). It conflicts on ign-sensors6. No Bazel change is needed because `test/BUILD.bazel` globs `sdf/**`.

WideAngleCameraSensor has the same gap. I left it out to keep this small and can follow up.
